title: Releases are SSH-signed `vX.Y.Z` tags on `main`, cut by `/preflight`, checked before the push as example-crew's channel checks them
body:
## ADR-026: Releases are SSH-signed `vX.Y.Z` tags on `main`, cut by `/preflight`, checked before the push as example-crew's channel checks them     (2026-09-16) — Accepted, Superseded in part by ADR-030

**Context:** example-crew is replacing its vendored mirror `image/harness/` (refreshed by hand and shipped by a crew release, governed by its ADR-062) with a host-side, signature-gated channel, a decision recorded in crew's handoff on 2026-09-16. A root timer on the crew host polls this repository for its newest SSH-signed tag, verifies it against `/etc/example/allowed_signers`, checks it out under `/var/lib/example/harness/<commit>/`, runs `sh-agent list` (expecting 27 skills and 7 agents) and `install --dry-run` into a scratch home, and atomically swaps a `current` link the server bind-mounts read-only. Tag selection and refusals follow crew's existing updater `deploy/update/example-update`: `git tag -l 'v*' | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | sort -V | tail -1`; lightweight tags are refused, and any tag whose last `BEGIN` armor header is not `BEGIN SSH SIGNATURE-----` is refused, because only git's SSH path consults the allowed-signers file. This repository carried no tag on 2026-09-16 (105 commits from root 9dcdc4c to 8b95f22); both downstream mirrors (example-crew and example-example-box) carry commit 4aa19be. The allowed signer, read with `sudo -n` from `/etc/example/allowed_signers` on 2026-09-16, is `op@example.invalid ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIExampleTestFixturePublicKey000000000000000` (the operator's `~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub`, fingerprint `SHA256:ExampleTestFixtureFingerprint000000000000000`); git 2.47.3 and OpenSSH 10.0 run on that Linux box, which also hosts crew's updater. The context's Git rule forbids an agent to change `git config`, force-push or rewrite history; "cut vX.Y.Z" from the operator's own turn means `/preflight`; a release adding behaviour is MINOR, one fixing released behaviour only is PATCH, MAJOR is reserved for what an existing deployment must react to. Signing was rehearsed in `.agents/scratch/tagcheck/` on 2026-09-16: per-command `-c gpg.format=ssh -c user.signingkey=...` flags work headless with no passphrase; `git verify-tag` against the allowed-signers line passes for the operator's key and fails with "No principal matched" for other keys; lightweight tags read as type `commit`; unsigned annotated tags fail with "no signature found"; verifying against `/etc/example/allowed_signers` itself fails with "Permission denied" for the operator user.

**Decision:** A release is an annotated tag `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` on `main`, SSH-signed with the operator's ed25519 key, pushed with a plain push; nothing else is a release and nothing else is tagged. Signing uses per-command flags, never a config change by an agent: `git -c gpg.format=ssh -c user.signingkey="$HOME/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub" tag -s vX.Y.Z -m "example-harness vX.Y.Z"` (no target argument). The operator may set `gpg.format` and `user.signingkey` in their own config; the procedure does not depend on it. The tag takes no target argument, so it sits on HEAD; before it is made, `test -z "$(git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all)"` (clean tree — the bare form inherits `status.showUntrackedFiles`, BUG-049), `test "$(git rev-parse HEAD^)" = "$(git rev-parse <gated head>)"` (the release commit sits on the head the gate report's `Range reviewed:` line names) and `git diff --quiet <gated head> HEAD -- ':(top)' ':(top,exclude).agents/docs'` (the release commit changed records only, so its source tree is the gated one — `:(top)` because a bare `.` is relative to the caller's directory and was measured missing a change in a sibling one) all exit 0; after it, `test "$(git rev-parse vX.Y.Z^{commit})" = "$(git rev-parse HEAD)"` and `git merge-base --is-ancestor vX.Y.Z^{commit} main` exit 0 (security review 2026-09-16: round 1 found no check of what the tag points at; round 2 found the first fix tautological because a `<release commit>` placeholder sat on both sides, so the target argument was deleted rather than defended). Then the tag is checked the way the consumer checks it, each assertion through `test` so its exit status carries the verdict: `git cat-file -t vX.Y.Z` prints `tag`; the last `BEGIN` line of `git cat-file tag vX.Y.Z` is `BEGIN SSH SIGNATURE-----` (a bare pipeline exits 0 either way); `git -c gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile=.agents/scratch/allowed_signers verify-tag vX.Y.Z` exits 0, the scratch file holding the one allowed-signers line quoted in `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md` (identical to the host file on 2026-09-16). The host file is the trust root; the quoted line adds no trust, since anyone who can push could change it, so on the crew host the scratch copy is compared with it first (`sudo -n cmp`, the only root step in the procedure and a read); `git` is never run under `sudo`. The signing machine proves it holds the private key with `ssh-keygen -y -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 | ssh-keygen -lf -`, not by the presence of a `.pub` file. A tag failing any check is deleted locally (`git tag -d`) and never pushed; a pushed tag is never moved or deleted. Version: MINOR for anything a consumer gains (a new or changed skill, agent, command, rule, context rule or installer behaviour), PATCH for a fix to released behaviour only, MAJOR for what an existing deployment must react to (a moved install path, a dropped vendor, a `state.json` or manifest shape change, a new required flag). The tag is the only version tracking; no version file is introduced. The first tag is `v1.0.0`, the harness having been in production use by two consumers since 2026-09-03; its gate's base ref is 4aa19be, the commit both consumers carry, so the release diff is what they have not seen. The cut is `/preflight vX.Y.Z` from the operator's own turn, on a machine holding the key (`ssh-keygen -y -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 | ssh-keygen -lf -` prints the fingerprint, derived from the private key), from the git checkout, never a mirror or plain copy. The gate's verification row is the project's Setup commands plus `go run ./cmd/sh-agent install --home .agents/scratch/home` with `status` reporting no drift and `sh-agent list`; a release changing those counts says so in its changelog entry. Preflight Step 6.5 (deploy) is nothing here: the push is the release, the consumer's timer does the rest, and its outcome is observed on the crew host, not from this repository. What a tag reaches: crew's channel only. `sh-agent update` on operator machines and on example-example-box keeps following `main`; a tag changes nothing for them; a `sh-agent update --release` that checks out the newest verified tag is a Feature question, not decided here. Until crew's channel ships, crew's mirror stays at 4aa19be and is not refreshed (crew's own decision in that handoff); example-example-box's mirror is refreshed as before.

title: An unsigned zip needs `--unverified`
body:
## ADR-040: An unsigned zip needs `--unverified`     (2026-09-28) — Superseded by ADR-041

**Context:** ADR-039 left one item open: a zip with neither `SHA256SUMS` nor `SHA256SUMS.sig` beside it still installed, marked `UNVERIFIED`, with exit 0. A marking discloses the risk but does not control it (security reviews 2026-09-28, medium, carried in `reviews/2026-09-28-preflight-v1.9.0.md` row 1). The docs gate also found R9's "a zip without them" imprecise, because a zip with only one of the two files was already refused (row 2). The v1.9.0 handoff proposed the exact R9 text, and the operator approved it: "Go approved all" (2026-09-28).

**Decision:**
- **Neither file beside the zip:** `update --from-zip` refuses the zip before a byte is written, and the refusal names `--unverified`. With `--unverified` it installs, marked `UNVERIFIED` in the output and `;unverified` in the manifest, as before.
- **The flag allows a MISSING signature, never a failed one.** One file alone, a bad signature, a stale pair or a checksum mismatch is refused with or without it.
- **The flag belongs to `update --from-zip` only.** Anywhere else it is refused, not ignored.
- A dry run refuses exactly as the real run does.

**Supersedes:** ADR-039's "`--from-zip` with nothing beside the zip installs it marked UNVERIFIED" and its Open bullet. R9's zip-place clause is replaced in the same commit.

**Rejected:**
- keeping the marking alone: it discloses and does not control;
- refusing every unsigned zip outright: it would remove R9's `main` zip path, which the operator uses on machines with no release to hand.

**Consequences:**
- A `main` zip now needs one more word on the command line.
- The refusal names the flag. That is not the bypass ADR-039 forbids, because the flag cannot pass a failed check, only a missing one; the refusals for failed checks still never mention it.
- The release carrying this is v2.0.0, a MAJOR. `deploy/remote.md`'s version rule names "a new required flag" as something an existing deployment must react to: a zip place that installs a `main` zip must now pass `--unverified`. A place that installs a release zip with its sums, a checkout, or a release-binary place is unaffected.

title: The zip place accepts the zip it is given
body:
## ADR-041: The zip place accepts the zip it is given     (2026-09-28) — Accepted

**Context:** ADR-040 made an unsigned zip need `--unverified` and refused a zip with only one of `SHA256SUMS`/`SHA256SUMS.sig` beside it. Its gate then raised further hardening: stray-argument refusals, agent-proof refusal wording, a downgrade check. The operator stopped that line before any release carried it: "Don't complicate things. Just accept the zip. This is a workaround for environments that can't use the normal way." (2026-09-28), then "Go approved allowed".

**Decision:**
**Supersedes:** ADR-040 whole, and ADR-039's "one file alone is refused" behaviour. R9's zip-place clause is restored to the v1.9.0 text ("a zip without them is installed marked `UNVERIFIED`"), which the code now matches exactly.
- `--unverified` (ADR-040): friction on the one path meant for machines where nothing else works;

title: A session is one Task or one plan phase; the handoff's Kickoff and `sh-agent kickoff` start the next
body:
## ADR-058: A session is one Task or one plan phase; the handoff's Kickoff and `sh-agent kickoff` start the next     (2026-10-23) — Accepted
**Context:** the operator asked twice (feedback log 2026-10-21, 2026-10-23) that work be split into session-sized chunks and that each session end with the prompt for the next; a repeated correction graduates into a mechanism. `plans/2026-10-23-research-session-sizing.md` measured 49 main Claude Code sessions since 2026-09-01 on this box: median peak context 573K tokens, 38 past 200K, 31 past 300K. The model cannot observe its own context, hooks are refused (R3, ADR-007) and no CLI lets anything outside a session run `/clear`, so the one boundary the model can see is the checkpoint it already writes. The hand-written context stood 71 bytes under its 15,000 pin, so the rule could not join it.
**Decision:** (1) `rules/session-sizing.md`, the harness's second always-on rule on both CLIs (beside `critical-thinking.md`, ADR-050), says a session is one Task or one plan phase, ends at its checkpoint with a handoff whose `## Kickoff` names the next session's work, and that a second unrelated ask, whatever its size, waits for its own Kickoff unless the operator's own words keep the session open (plan D2, D11, D31). (2) The handoff template gains `## Kickoff`: a fenced, paste-ready prompt whose standing approvals are a closed set written in the template and never extended by the agent (D3, D17); one line when nothing is queued; printed in chat only in an unscaffolded project (D18). (3) `sh-agent kickoff` prints the newest handoff's block for the checkout the shell is in, exit 1 with `kickoff: nothing queued` on stderr and nothing on stdout when none, so `claude "$(sh-agent kickoff)"` or `agy -i "$(sh-agent kickoff)"` starts the next session (D28, D32: Antigravity takes an initial interactive prompt only through `-i`); it is a consult verb under R0, reads no home and no harness tree (its global flags are refused, the BUG-171 shape), and moves nothing onto a machine, so the README map does not change (project `AGENTS.md` rule 3 does not apply). The headless loop is a documented one-liner, not a verb (D29). (4) The feature skill sizes a phase to what one fresh session finishes and verifies from the plan alone, its cold read asks a fourth question (sizing), and its checkpoint sentence ends the session (D9). (5) The context target is 300,000 tokens as a flag default on `sh-agent metrics show|report`, tuned by `/retro` from the metric, never a pin (D4, D15, D27); the metric itself is the plan's Phase 2, and the plan runs under its own rule from Phase 1 on.
**Consequences:** every phase boundary costs a resume (about 30K tokens; accepted, the plan's Follow-ups name the fix: `bugs/INDEX.md` is read whole). Definition of Done step 5 ends the session instead of recommending it. A CLI that ignores the rule shows in the § 4 behavioural run as n of N, never hidden (ADR-050 records one Antigravity run where the first rule did not hold). The rule shares the 22,000-byte Antigravity block (`TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock`). ADR-059 (reviewer isolation, D10) and ADR-060 (the auto-compact backstop, D25) stay reserved by the plan.

title: Antigravity silently dropped the `bug` and `feature` skills
body:
# BUG-004: Antigravity silently dropped the `bug` and `feature` skills

## Prevention
The lenient parser is not the reference; the vendors' strict parsers are. After any frontmatter change, install into the sandbox home, run each CLI once, and grep its log for parse errors — `sh-agent status` says the files match, not that the vendor read them.

title: `verifier` ran in a fresh worktree and could not see uncommitted work
body:
# BUG-005: `verifier` ran in a fresh worktree and could not see uncommitted work

## Prevention
A Claude-only agent key is not free: `isolation: worktree` is only right for an agent that must work on a committed base, never for one that judges uncommitted work. Any change to an agent's frontmatter is followed by one dispatch in the sandbox on an uncommitted change.

title: `sh-agent install` kept the operator's real `~/.local/bin/sh-agent` stuck on the 2026-09-03 build
body:
# BUG-006: `sh-agent install` kept the operator's real `~/.local/bin/sh-agent` stuck on the 2026-09-03 build

## Prevention
A self-updating tool that copies "itself" runs its OLD code on the very tick meant to install the change — the same shape as example-crew's BUG-035 and the review-standards §2 "installers count as callers" paragraph. Any installer that copies its own running binary must instead build from source, and `status` must compare the running build's stamp against the repo. After any change to `cmd/` or `internal/`, run `sh-agent status` from the real home and read the `binary` line before calling the install done.

title: agent-name shadowing defeats the independent review rows
body:
# BUG-033: agent-name shadowing defeats the independent review rows

## Prevention
Before dispatching `reviewer`, `security`, `verifier`, or `explorer` for an independent judgement, list `.claude/agents/` and `.agents/agents/` (and the diff's changed paths there) for a name clash with a harness review agent; a clash stops the dispatch and is blocking in `/preflight` Step 5, not just Step 2.

title: Claude Code headless commits carried a Co-Authored-By trailer despite the no-attribution rule
body:
# BUG-039: Claude Code headless commits carried a Co-Authored-By trailer despite the no-attribution rule

## Prevention
A rule that overrides a CLI's built-in behaviour must name the CLI's own setting for it and the command
that reports the setting missing — prose alone does not hold against a vendor-injected reminder. Before
writing a "never do X" rule about agent-emitted output, check whether X is actually a tool/vendor default
rather than a choice the agent is making.

title: security agent graded stdlib crypto/rand UUID generation as hand-rolled cryptography
body:
# BUG-041: security agent graded stdlib crypto/rand UUID generation as hand-rolled cryptography

## Prevention
A ban must name the thing banned precisely enough that its stdlib counterpart is not caught by it.
When two harness agents contradict each other on the same mechanism in the same round, the rule is the
defect, not the code — fix the rule before trusting either report.

title: `sh-agent update` reinstalled an uncommitted, dirty checkout
body:
# BUG-046: `sh-agent update` reinstalled an uncommitted, dirty checkout

## Prevention
`update` refuses a dirty checkout on every path, not just "behind
upstream" — graduated into `cmd/sh-agent/main.go`, `ADR-027`, and
`REQUIREMENTS.md` R4. Before relying on `sh-agent update` on a checkout used
for active development, confirm the dirty check itself is pinned (see
BUG-049): a guard that trusts git's configurable default can still pass a
dirty-looking-clean tree.

Graduated to: `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` `update()` (refuses a dirty checkout on every path); ADR-027; `REQUIREMENTS.md` R4

title: the documented gate `gofmt -l .` fails on junk left in `.agents/scratch`
body:
# BUG-048: the documented gate `gofmt -l .` fails on junk left in `.agents/scratch`

## Prevention
A verification command that walks the whole tree is scoped to the source
directories on any project that keeps generated files under
`.agents/scratch/`; `agents/verifier.md` § What to run now names this caveat
for its Go auto-detect so the rule reaches every project, not just this one.

Graduated to: `agents/verifier.md` § What to run, plus `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `.agents/docs/deploy/local.md`, `.agents/docs/testing/sh-agent/guide.md` (`gofmt -l cmd internal`)

title: the BUG-046 dirty-checkout guard trusted git's configurable default
body:
# BUG-049: the BUG-046 dirty-checkout guard trusted git's configurable default

## Prevention
A guard never trusts a git command's default when a config key can change
it — pass the flag that pins the behaviour, and test with that key set
against you.

Graduated to: `internal/harness/repo.go` (`--untracked-files=all`) and `TestInspectCountsUntrackedFiles`

title: a secret in a JSON key was written verbatim into `report.json` as the redaction's recorded path
body:
# BUG-054: a secret in a JSON key was written verbatim into `report.json` as the redaction's recorded path

## Prevention
A test that verifies redaction correctness must assert on content (the marshalled/sent bytes contain no secret), not just record count — `len(recs) == 1` proves a record was made, not that it is safe. When a field is meant to carry metadata only (a path, a location), assert directly that it never carries the value it points at.

title: verifier dispatched against a tree the main agent kept editing
body:
# BUG-072: verifier dispatched against a tree the main agent kept editing

## Prevention
While a `verifier` dispatch is in flight, do not edit any file in its scope — keep
the tree frozen until the artifact lands; note anything found meanwhile and apply
it after. When a fix cannot wait, stop the run (TaskStop) rather than let it verify
a moving tree, then dispatch again after committing.

Graduated to: `context/AGENTS.md` § Definition of Done, step 1, "While that dispatch is IN FLIGHT the tree stays frozen" sentence

title: release binary silently installed a stale plain-copy tree instead of its embedded harness
body:
# BUG-077: release binary silently installed a stale plain-copy tree instead of its embedded harness

## Prevention
When a program can obtain the same input from several sources, decide the order per KIND of
build, not once for all of them — an artifact that ships its own copy of an input must never
silently prefer a copy it found on the machine, and a source that cannot be updated (a plain
copy) is never preferred over one that can. State which source won whenever more than one was
possible and the choice changes what the tool then deploys.

title: relative `--home` resolved against the repo directory on a real install, against cwd on `--dry-run`
body:
# BUG-080: relative `--home` resolved against the repo directory on a real install, against cwd on `--dry-run`

## Prevention
A path handed to a child process started with a different working directory (`cmd.Dir`) is made absolute before the handoff — the child cannot know the parent's cwd. This is also an instance of the `context/AGENTS.md` read-only-mode rule: `--dry-run` must resolve paths exactly as the real run does, or it is not a dry run of the real run.

Graduated to: `context/AGENTS.md` § Hard rules, "When a command has a read-only mode" bullet

title: Antigravity loads only the first 24,000 bytes of the deployed global context
body:
# BUG-085: Antigravity loads only the first 24,000 bytes of the deployed global context

## Prevention
A deployed file that a vendor caps is pinned by a test that renders it from the real repo against the observed cap with a margin. Every smoke check asks one question answerable ONLY from the file's last section — never a question (like a skill count) the CLI can answer from its own internal listing, because that gives a false pass on a truncated file.

title: installer piped into `head` was killed by SIGPIPE, leaving files with no manifest
body:
# BUG-086: installer piped into `head` was killed by SIGPIPE, leaving files with no manifest

## Prevention
Never pipe a command that has side effects (install, update, report, a git write) into a filter that can exit before consuming its output (`head`, `grep -q`, `grep -m1`, `sed q`); run it bare, redirect its output to a file under `.agents/scratch/` if it must be shortened, and read that file. Recommend widening the existing `context/AGENTS.md` § Hard rules sentence "A verification command is never piped into a filter inside a `&&` chain that leads to a commit…" with one clause covering a side-effecting command piped into an early-exiting filter, rather than a new bullet — the rendered context is size-pinned at 22,000 bytes (ADR-035, `TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock`).

Graduated to: `review-standards § 8 (code-shape rules; the reviewer's criterion, and golang/typescript/bash point at it)`

title: verifier grep needle didn't match the sentence it was checking
body:
# BUG-097: verifier grep needle didn't match the sentence it was checking

## Prevention
Before dispatching a verifier check built on a grep, the main agent runs that grep bare on the working tree in the must-pass state first — this is the existing global rule ("a check is validated once in the must-pass and once in the must-fail state before its verdict is cited") applied to the dispatch-authoring step, which was skipped here. This is a test failing for a reason other than the change under test and cost one extra verifier round.

title: dreamer sampled `bugs/INDEX.md` and missed the newest rows
body:
# BUG-100: dreamer sampled `bugs/INDEX.md` and missed the newest rows

## Prevention
An agent told to read an index states the bound explicitly (a date, or "all") and says "every row", never "recent rows" — an unbounded instruction over a growing table is read as a sample.

title: an empty slug from a failed `git rev-parse` made the store the shared root, and migration ran even when the settings write was refused
body:
# BUG-103: an empty slug from a failed `git rev-parse` made the store the shared root, and migration ran even when the settings write was refused

## Prevention
A step that derives a path from a project file or a command's output checks the result (non-empty, well-formed) before any move; a step that depends on a prior write's success checks that write succeeded before acting on its result, never assuming order implies success.

title: `update --vendor bogus` pulled the checkout before refusing, and other verbs exited 1 or 0
body:
# BUG-171: `update --vendor bogus` pulled the checkout before refusing, and other verbs exited 1 or 0

## Prevention
A flag registered on every verb is validated once, before the verb dispatch, not where each verb first reads it. A usage check that sits after a side effect (a fetch, a pull, a write) is a bug even when its exit code is right, and the read-only mode of a verb resolves the same check (review-standards § 8).

title: `sh-agent update --from-zip`: a third way in, the zip place (date: 2026-09-28)
v1.9.0 gate findings fixed before the tag (date: 2026-09-28)
body:
# v1.9.0 gate findings fixed before the tag     (date: 2026-09-28)

## Summary
Every low finding from the v1.9.0 gate reviews over `v1.8.0..52cebd8` is fixed before the tag. None was blocking; the operator said "All needs to be fixed".

`internal/harness/release.go`, `internal/harness/zip.go` (comment), `cmd/sh-agent/main.go`, `internal/harness/zip_test.go`, `cmd/sh-agent/zip_test.go`, `README.md`, `context/AGENTS.md`, `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/delivery.md`; the `## Outcome` sections of `reviews/2026-09-28-review-v1.8.0-52cebd8-code.md` and `reviews/2026-09-28-security-v1.8.0-52cebd8.md`.

title: Release v1.10.0 (date: 2026-09-28)
body:
# Release v1.10.0     (date: 2026-09-28)

## Summary
v1.10.0 is gated SHIP over `v1.9.0..e33a4e1` (`reviews/2026-09-28-preflight-v1.10.0.md`).

- **Decision records:** ADR-040 (an `--unverified` flag) was added and superseded by ADR-041 within this release, and was never shipped.

title: v2.7.0 gate fixes: BUG-171, the dream signal relay, the timer's home, redaction kinds, disallowedTools off the allow-list (2026-10-12)
body:
# v2.7.0 gate fixes: BUG-171, the dream signal relay, the timer's home, redaction kinds, disallowedTools off the allow-list     (2026-10-12)

## Summary
The release gate's reviewer and security agents reviewed v2.6.2..13c5bde. Nothing blocked; every finding was low. The operator chose what went in. Round 1 fixes:
- **BUG-171:** a bad `--vendor` is a usage error, exit 2, for every verb before the verb does anything. Before, `update` fetched and pulled the checkout first and exited 1, `--dry-run` never checked the value, `status` exited 1, and `uninstall` and `report` took any word.
- `cmd/sh-agent/main.go`, `main_test.go`, `usage_test.go` — BUG-171: one `--vendor` check before the verb dispatch; `TestUpdateRefusesABadVendorFirst` (a fixture checkout one commit behind its local origin; `advanceOrigin` made package-level), three `TestUsageErrorsExit2` rows
- `.agents/docs/bugs/BUG-171-*.md`, `INDEX.md`

title: fyr Phase 2: Claude Code leaves the binary (date: 2026-10-24)
body:
# fyr Phase 2: Claude Code leaves the binary     (date: 2026-10-24)

## Summary
`sh-agent` installs into the Antigravity CLI only (ADR-062, plan `2026-10-24-fyr-agy-only.md` Phase 2, D7, D14, D17). `Plan` and `Install` lost their vendor argument. Nothing is planned or written under `~/.claude`, and the `CLAUDE.md` stub is gone. `--vendor` is gone from every verb, so passing it is a usage error, exit 2. `~/.claude/settings.json` is never read or written: `settings.go` is deleted, so the attribution and auto-compact keys an older install wrote stay as the operator's. An install over an older manifest sheds that manifest's `~/.claude` files through the existing resync, unchanged. A symlink, or a path under a linked directory, stays, and `~/.claude` itself stays in `pruneEmptyDirs`' stop map. `memory show` prints the index only. `dream` always runs `agy`, reads skills from `~/.gemini/config/skills` and reads transcripts from Antigravity's conversations only. `metrics ingest` reads Antigravity only. `show`, `report` and the dream summary have one `agy` column. A second column, `claude (historical)`, appears only when the window holds rows an older ingest stored (D7). Nothing deletes those rows, and `export` writes them as before.

## Type
task (plan phase)

## Files changed
from `git diff --numstat` (+1,172 −1,784 in the working tree, deleted files included)
- Deleted: `internal/harness/settings.go`, `internal/harness/settings_test.go`, `cmd/sh-agent/settings_test.go`, `internal/metrics/claude.go`, `internal/metrics/claude_test.go`
- `internal/harness/plan.go`: one target. `VendorAll`, `VendorClaude`, `NormalizeVendor`, `KeepForeign`, `IsOurs` and `ClaudeRoot` are gone. `VendorAntigravity` stays, so the manifest still records it.
- `internal/harness/apply.go`: `Install(src, home, files, dryRun, out)`. The foreign-file branches are gone. The stop map names `~/.claude` as a literal, with the reason beside it.
- `internal/harness/{render,state,adopt,inventory,frontmatter}.go`: the stub constant goes. The manifest's `Vendor` is written `antigravity`, and an old value is read and ignored. `adopt` no longer looks in `~/.claude/skills`. Comments changed.
- `cmd/sh-agent/main.go`: the `--vendor` flag, `resolveVendor`, `ctx.vendor`, the settings calls, the foreign-`CLAUDE.md` note and the `claude` status line are gone. `installPassArgs` forwards `--home` alone. Usage text changed.
- `internal/memory/memory.go`: `Show(dir)`. The native-memory hint and `nativeOn` are gone.
- `internal/dream/{dream,collect,run,metrics,timer}.go`: `command()` is agy-only, and the private HOME and the stream-json stdin are unconditional. `answer(stdout)`. The Claude transcript reader is gone. The summary counts sessions over every column.
- `internal/metrics`: `writer.go` is new and holds the writer helpers `agy.go` shares, moved verbatim from `claude.go`. `ingest.go` reads agy only. `show.go` has `Columns` and the `historical` column, with lazily made count maps. `numbers.go` and `report.go` follow the columns; the report's series and tables are built per summary, and Antigravity keeps colour slot 2. `store.go` and `agy.go` comments changed.
- `internal/search/dream.go`: one comment.
- Tests, new: `TestPlanAntigravityOnly`, `TestResyncShedsOldClaudeFiles`, `TestInstallLeavesClaudeCodeAlone`, `TestUpdateRefusesTheVendorFlagFirst` (BUG-171's rule, kept for the flag that no longer exists), `TestInstallPassArgsForwardsTheHomeOnly`, the six `--vendor agy` rows of `TestUsageErrorsExit2`, `TestShowHistoricalColumn`, `TestShowAgyOnly`, `TestReportAgyOnly`, `TestAgyIdentifiersAreNameShaped`, `TestIngestPrintsNoControlOrFormatCharacters`.
- Tests, moved onto Antigravity fixtures: `TestSourceLabelAndOutcome`, `TestOutcomeStampedAfterTheRun`, `TestMetricsVerb` (with a decoy `HOME`, for R6), every dream run test (`fakeAgy`), and the dream collect tests (`agyConversations`, whose schema both readers accept).
- Tests, historical: `historical_test.go`'s `historicalRows` inserts what an old ingest stored, for the show, report and numbers tests.
- Tests, deleted: the Claude transcript, settings, stub, foreign-`CLAUDE.md`, vendor-selection and native-memory-hint tests.
- Docs (the `documentation` agent): `README.md`, `specs/sh-agent/{metrics,memory-loop,dream}.md`, `deploy/{local,remote}.md`, `testing/guide.md`. `memory-loop.md` § Known differences is retired. Main agent: `AGENTS.md` lines 7, 39 and 44, and one `memory-loop.md` phrase.
- Plan: Phase 2's two work boxes are ticked. The checkpoint stays open (below).

## Deviations from the plan's box
- **The checkpoint's grep is met in part.** `git grep -il claude -- 'cmd' 'internal' '*.go'` lists 17 files. Expected among them: the stop-map entry (`apply.go`, with the resync comment of `Install`), the historical column (`main.go:65` and `internal/metrics/{ingest,report,show,store}.go` with their tests) and the stop-map tests. Not expected:
  - the Claude Code agent format: `derive.go`, `inventory.go` lines 23, 225 and 234, and `harness_test.go` lines 43, 155, 2351–2371 and 2439. Phase 3a deletes it (D3, D17).
  - the listing-budget comments: `catalog_test.go:671` and `size_test.go:90`. The 19,500-byte budget rests on Claude Code's listing; Antigravity's is about 44,000.
  - `internal/search/testdata/recall.tsv` rows 19 and 39 (D20).
  The box stays open until Phase 3a lands or the operator amends it.
- The "tests first" red was a build failure of the old tests against the new API in six packages, not a test-by-test red. Each removed symbol appears in `.agents/scratch/fyr/go-test-phase2-red.txt`.
- `State.Vendor` is still written, as `antigravity`, rather than dropped. `skills/init-project` and `skills/dream` grep for it until Phase 3b removes the check.
- `metrics.DefaultContextTarget` keeps 300,000. Its other half, the auto-compact window, went with `settings.go`, and so did `TestAutoCompactWindowIsTheContextTarget`.
- The `testing/guide.md` three-sandbox kit (§ 4, Claude Code runs) is left for Phase 3b. `memory-loop.md`'s `/init-project` rows are the skill's, also Phase 3b.

## Agents dispatched
- `documentation`: the README, specs, deploy and testing-guide edits. Its diff was read against the code by the main agent. One claim it kept ("Antigravity prompts … for paths outside the workspace") was already in the old text.
- The plan's Phase 5 holds the Definition of Done over the whole feature: the `verifier` log, `reviewer --code --docs` and `security`. This phase's code diff was read by the main agent only.

## Verification
- Full suite: `gofmt -l cmd internal` empty, `go vet ./...` ok, `go test -race -count=1 -timeout 30m ./...` exit 0, all 9 packages ok (`.agents/scratch/fyr/go-test-phase2.txt`). It ran on go1.24.4 (`~/.local/bin/go` still dangles). `govulncheck` reports the same 15 standard-library advisories as Phase 1, all fixed in later Go (`.agents/scratch/fyr/govulncheck-p2.txt`).
- Fresh scratch home (`.agents/scratch/fyr/home-p2`): `go run ./cmd/sh-agent install --home …` exit 0, 896 files, and no `.claude` directory. The installed binary's `status` exits 0 with `drift none — 895 files match the repo`, and the `binary` line has no warning. The `installed` line no longer prints a vendor.
- Crossing, local half (`.agents/scratch/fyr/home-p2-old`):
  - The `HEAD` build (from `git archive a60f83a`) installed 897 files under `.claude`, 896 of them in its manifest, and created `settings.json`.
  - This tree's install then exited 0 with `896 removed`, each reported as `remove  ~/.claude/… (no longer in the source)`.
  - `~/.claude` and `settings.json` stayed, untouched. The new manifest has vendor `antigravity` and no `.claude` entry, and `status` reports `drift none`.
- The usage rows prove that `--vendor agy` exits 2 with `flag provided but not defined: -vendor` on install, status, uninstall, dream, memory show, metrics ingest and update (checkout, dry run, zip). No checkout moved.

## Docs
Every file above. The map's node labels changed text only: no line or node was added, removed or rerouted (rule 3), and `TestHarnessMap` passes. The ADR is ADR-062.

title: Deploy — local (this machine)
body:
# Deploy — local (this machine)

"Deploying" the harness means installing the context, skills, and agents into a home directory. Development never touches the real `$HOME` (`PRD.md` R6); deploying to it is the operator's action.

## Prerequisites

Go 1.24+ and git. `~/.local/bin` on `PATH`. The Antigravity CLI (`agy`) installed; it is the only target. The installer writes only under `~/.gemini/config/` and `~/.local/bin` and edits no vendor setting (PRD.md § Non-goals, ADR-062); `--vendor` is a usage error.

## Build and install

```bash
cd ~/workspace/fyr   # the checkout; a place cloned before the rename keeps its directory name
gofmt -l cmd internal && go vet ./... && go test -race -timeout 30m ./...   # before deploying anything; gofmt takes the source dirs, not `.` (it walks .agents/scratch, BUG-048); -timeout 30m for a one-CPU box (cmd/fyr ~13 min under -race)
go run ./cmd/fyr install                             # builds the binary from this checkout, writes ~/.gemini/config, installs the build to ~/.local/bin/fyr
fyr status                                           # must end with "drift none"
```

The worker image for `fyr work --runner docker` (optional; Docker, or Colima on the Mac): the build line is `SPEC-fyr-work` § The worker image. Rebuild it after every `fyr install` that changes the binary, because the verb will refuse an image stamped with another version (Phase 7b-2).

## Update

```bash
fyr update                 # fetch; refuse a dirty checkout; if behind: pull --ff-only; rebuild and reinstall
fyr update --check         # only reports; exit 2 when behind
```

The normal way a checkout moves forward, run whenever the operator decides the harness has changed; `remote.md` § The resync loop covers the timer and the dirty-checkout refusal.

## Update a release-binary install

A place installed from a release binary (README § Install without cloning) has no checkout and nothing to build from, so `update` moves it to the newest RELEASE instead (which place gets what from a tag: `SPEC-fyr-delivery` § The model):

```bash
fyr update --check         # only reports; exit 2 when a newer release exists
fyr update                 # download the newest release, verify it, replace ~/.local/bin/fyr, reinstall
```

What it does, in order: asks `gh` for the newest release's tag; refuses anything that is not a `vX.Y.Z` tag, and anything not numerically newer than the installed version — nothing but this check stops a downgrade to an older, genuine release; downloads this platform's binary with `SHA256SUMS` into a temporary directory under `~/.config/fyr/`, removed on every path out; checks that `SHA256SUMS` names this release and that the binary matches its line in it (integrity only; no key signs a release, ADR-053); and only then replaces `~/.local/bin/fyr` through a rename and runs the new binary's `install`. Any failure leaves the installed binary untouched and names the check that failed. It needs `gh` on `PATH`; a development build is never overwritten from a release.

## From a plain copy (no `.git`)

A copy of the repository with no `.git` — for a major remodel, or a machine that cannot authenticate to GitHub. It needs Go, and the Go module proxy or a filled module cache for the one dependency, `modernc.org/sqlite` (ADR-045):

```bash
cd <unpacked directory>
go run ./cmd/fyr install             # installs the running binary as is; never rebuilds (BUG-015)
fyr status                           # first line names a plain copy with no commit; must end with "drift none"
```

`fyr update` refuses a plain copy, by design, with a message naming `install` still deploying it as it is and the alternatives. To move it forward, unpack a newer copy and run `install` from it again; to roll back, install the earlier one. This path is not one of the ways in — `SPEC-fyr-delivery` § The model names the three (a checkout, a release binary, a zip place — `README.md` § Install from a zip (no SSH, no gh)) and this plain copy as their fallback; it stays because the code path does and because it is the fallback when none of the three can reach GitHub.

## What stays on this machine

Nothing is sent from this machine but the dreamer's redacted prompt (below), `fyr eval`'s runs (started by you or, when `fyr auto` is turned on at level `harness`, by its hourly run), and the `fyr work` workers you start or that `fyr auto` starts when you turn it on, plus a `missing-skill` worker's search of `skills.sh` with the pinned CLI (`SPEC-fyr-delivery` § What stays on the machine). The `report` verb is gone (ADR-062): the brain store `brain.db` (the global feedback, proposal and retro records), the search index and the metrics store stay in `~/.config/fyr/`, and a harness-target proposal reaches the harness checkout only through `/retro --harness`, run there by you, or, when `fyr auto` is turned on at level `harness`, as an eval-gated commit to a skill or agent in that checkout, never pushed (ADR-090). An older version left two things no verb removes any more: a kept clone at `~/.config/fyr/feedback` (versions before the throwaway clone) and a `~/.config/fyr/report-<pid>` directory after an interrupted run. Each is a clone of the feedback repository; read what it holds, then delete it by hand.

## The background dreamer (optional, once per machine)

```bash
fyr dream --install-timer        # systemd user timer (Linux) or launchd agent (macOS): fyr dream --all hourly, while an agy session of yours runs
fyr status                       # its line: dream      last run <date>: <n> projects, <m> proposals; timer installed
fyr dream --all --dry-run        # what each registered project would send (an unregistered one: skip not registered), and the CLI command; writes nothing
fyr dream --remove-timer         # stop and remove it (uninstall does too)
```

- The unit runs `~/.local/bin/fyr`, with the absolute entries of the PATH of the shell that ran `--install-timer`, so it finds `agy` there; one reachable only through a relative PATH entry is not found when the timer fires. Run it from the shell you work in. A rerun from a shell with another PATH renders other text: the installed unit is kept and named, so run `--remove-timer` first.
- The unit is `fyr-dream.timer` (Linux) or `com.fyr.dream` (macOS) for the real home and carries a short hash suffix for any other `--home`. It runs `dream --all --home <that home>`, so a scratch install or removal leaves the real timer alone and a scratch timer never dreams over the real home (the service manager is shared by every home of the user; BUG-144). The real home is the account's home in the account database, never `HOME`. A unit under the names from before v3.0.0 is no longer read, replaced, removed or named by any verb: every place crossed (ledger A1, D40; Phase 10).
- The dream job always runs `agy` (plan mode, the prompt on stdin); with no `agy` on PATH it fails before the first project.
- Antigravity needs the operator's login: on Linux `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/antigravity-oauth-token`, which agy uses in place in the visible branch (under `--home`) and which the private branch (`SPEC-fyr-dream` step 4) copies into a private HOME under `~/.config/fyr/dream-agy-home-*`; on macOS agy keeps it in the Keychain, so the run links `~/Library/Keychains` into that HOME instead (and copies the token file too when one exists), so the dream job's agy shares the operator's real Keychain login: a refresh it makes reaches the interactive agy too. The HOME is removed after the run; a locked Keychain (no user logged in to the Mac) makes agy ask for a browser login, which it gives up on after its own 60-second wait, so each project fails in about a minute with `agy is not logged in inside the dream job's private HOME` (BUG-166).
- A project is dreamt over only once `fyr index --register` has run in it (the operator's consent, ADR-068); which registered projects a run takes is `SPEC-fyr-dream`'s.
- On Linux a user timer fires only while your user manager runs (a login, or `loginctl enable-linger`). example-host has `Linger=yes` (`loginctl show-user $USER -p Linger`, 2026-11-01), so the dream's timer, and `fyr auto`'s when turned on (`observe` on example-host from 2026-11-01), fire while the operator is logged out. `Persistent=true` runs a missed hour at the next login. A timer an older fyr installed keeps its nightly 03:00 schedule, and with the session check it dreams only when an `agy` session of yours runs at 03:00, which is almost never; `fyr status` says so: run `fyr dream --remove-timer`, then `fyr dream --install-timer`.
- Every real run first runs `fyr metrics ingest`. It reads the shape of Antigravity sessions into `~/.config/fyr/metrics.db` (never sent anywhere; `uninstall` keeps it) and logs its summary line to `dream.log`. Each project's prompt then carries a numbers-only summary of its metrics. The store is the only copy once Antigravity deletes a transcript, so back it up now and then with `fyr metrics export <file>`. Look at it with `fyr metrics show` or `fyr metrics report` (spec `SPEC-fyr-metrics`).
- Output: global `proposal` records in `brain.db`, `Dream, project — …` per project and `Dream, harness — …` for harness targets, which wait for `/retro --harness`; draft skills under `~/.config/fyr/proposals/dream/drafts/`. A failed project's output goes to `dream-failed/`, and the log is `dream.log`. Nothing is applied until `/retro` does it.

## Auto-mode (optional, once per machine)

```bash
fyr auto on --level observe      # writes ~/.config/fyr/auto.json (0600) and installs fyr-auto.timer (Linux) or com.fyr.auto (macOS)
fyr auto status                  # level and thresholds, last run and gate verdicts, today's model runs (n of 4), open asks
fyr auto run --dry-run           # prints each gate's verdict per registered project and the task class it would choose; writes nothing
fyr auto off                     # writes enabled: false with no lock and removes the timer (uninstall removes the timer too)
```

- Runs `fyr auto run` hourly from `~/.local/bin/fyr` with the absolute `PATH` entries of the shell that ran `fyr auto on` (`Nice=19`, `IOSchedulingClass=idle`, `RandomizedDelaySec=10m`, `ConditionACPower=true`, `TimeoutStartSec=3h` on Linux; `ProcessType=Background`, `LowPriorityIO`, `Nice=15` on macOS; spec `SPEC-fyr-auto`, ADR-090).
- Trust ramp on example-host (`PLAN-2026-10-31-1636-plan-fyr-auto-mode-idle-time-self-improvement-of` Phase 8): turned on at `--level observe` on 2026-11-01 (`project_idle` 6h, `user_idle` 15m; free health checks and global `review` report records only, no model calls and no project writes). Raising the level (`project`, then `harness`) requires the operator's word after reading the report records.

## Configure

Nothing to configure. The global flags are `--repo` and `--home`; `--vendor` is gone and any use of it is a usage error on every verb, exit 2 (`flag provided but not defined: -vendor`). The manifest still records `"vendor": "antigravity"`; an older value is read and ignored. `--repo DIR` overrides where the checkout is; `$FYR_REPO` does the same persistently (an `SH_AGENT_*` variable is ignored, with a notice on stderr). Without either, install and update discover the checkout by walking up from the working directory, then fall back to the path recorded at the last install; when that discovery finds a checkout OTHER than the one already on record — an unpacked copy, a second clone sitting in a harness-shaped directory — the build is refused rather than run and deployed: `"checkout %s is not the installed one (%s); pass --repo %s to build and install from it"`, or, on a release-binary install, `"this home was installed from the release binary %s, not from a checkout; pass --repo %s to build and install from it"`. `--home DIR` installs elsewhere and is what every development run uses (a scratch home under `.agents/scratch/`, never `/tmp`). From its own git checkout, `install` rebuilds the binary with `go build` first; the running binary is installed as is when `go` is missing (with a warning) or when the tree is a plain copy with no `.git` — an unpacked bundle (BUG-015).

## Verify

- `fyr status` shows the current commit, a `binary` line carrying the same revision (a warning there means the installed binary is older than the checkout or unstamped: run `fyr update`), and no drift, with no `shadowed` line — a checkout place can be shadowed the same way a release-binary place was (BUG-078). `fyr version` run unqualified must match what was just installed; if it does not, `hash -r` (bash) or `rehash` (zsh) first — the shell caches where it last found `fyr`, and `update` replaces only `~/.local/bin/fyr` (BUG-079; `update` says so when it ran from another copy, but only against the real home, never `--home` elsewhere — remedy is `ln -sfn` to the installed binary when that copy is yours, or, when it is not, removing it with the rights that own it or running the installed one by its path) — and if still wrong, an earlier `fyr` on `PATH` is running instead of the installed one (`type fyr` shows which). `status` shows one `agy  ~/.gemini/config …` line, no `(vendor: …)` text and no settings note.
- `fyr render | head -3` prints the assembled context.
- Start Antigravity once and check it read the files: `/skills` and `/agents` list the harness entries, and `grep 'Failed to parse' ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/log/cli-*.log` is empty (BUG-004).

## First session after install

Antigravity prompts once per session for paths outside the workspace, such as the first read or write under `~/.config/fyr/` (the brain store `brain.db`, which holds the global `feedback`, `proposal` and `retro` records, and the metrics store `metrics.db`); approve it. The installer touches no vendor setting file (ADR-062). A project's memory is not a file in the project: `fyr memory add` writes it as `memory` records in the brain store, `~/.config/fyr/brain.db`, keyed by the main worktree's root (`SPEC-fyr-memory-loop`).

## agy models and quota (before every agy dispatch)

The operator's rule (`rules/agy-dispatch.md`): before scheduling `fyr work`, choose each worker's model by tier and pass it with `--model`. Before that and before every `fyr eval` run, read the quota, then state the tier, the model and the quota left in one line per dispatch. A model out means a similar model in the same tier, named with why. A tier out means stop and ask; never a weaker tier.

- **Quota:** `agy -p "/usage"` (the same as `/quota`), run outside every checkout; `--output-format json` gives `command.data.groups[].buckets[]` with `remaining_fraction` and `reset_time`. It starts no agent turn, spends no quota and leaves no conversation (agy changelog; on 2026-10-31 it gave 0 turns, 0 tokens).
- **Models:** `agy models` lists them, and `agy -p "/model"` prints the default.
- **Pools:** quota is per pool, not per model. Each pool has a weekly limit and a 5-hour limit, charged by token cost, so when a pool is out every tier in it is out.

Tiers on example-host, agy 1.4.12, 2026-10-31:

| Tier | Models | Pool |
|---|---|---|
| [pro] | `gemini-4-argon-low`, `-medium`, `-high` | Gemini Models |
| [flash] | `gemini-3.8-flash-low`, `-medium`, `-high` | Gemini Models |
| [opus] | `claude-opus-5-5-low`, `-medium`, `-high` | Claude and GPT models |
| [sonnet] | `claude-sonnet-5-5-low`, `-medium`, `-high` | Claude and GPT models |
| [gpt-oss] | `gpt-oss-120b-medium` | Claude and GPT models |

- **The tiers' source:** `/usage` names the Gemini pool's families "Gemini Flash, Gemini Pro". Argon is [pro] by elimination, an inference.
- **No [plan] tier:** "plan" in the rule is the scheduling step.
- **`fyr eval`'s model:** it has no `--model`, so it runs the account default, `gemini-4-argon-medium` ([pro]). The real `settings.json` sets no model, and the eval home's sessions recorded `gemini-4-argon`.
- **Refresh:** re-run `agy models` when agy is updated, and update this table.

## Operator steps

Standing by-hand procedures on this box, never pending items (those live in the newest handoff):

- After a push from another machine: `fyr update`, then `fyr status` shows a stamped `binary` line and no drift.
- Keep example-host current (standing permission, the operator, 2026-10-29): on example-host, every session's checkpoint ends, after its commit and push and on a clean tree only, with `fyr install` from this checkout into the real home. Then `fyr status` must show a `binary` line without a warning and `drift none`, and the handoff quotes both lines. A dirty tree, a failing suite or an unpushed commit means no install, and the handoff says why. A lead (`work` skill) defers it to its closing handoff's Next Steps, for the final tree (ADR-077). The smoke checks below remain the operator's.
- After the upgrade to opt-in registration (ADR-068): `fyr dream --dry-run --all` lists every indexed project it now skips as `not registered`; run `fyr index --register` in each project you want the dream, `search --global`, `record import --global` and the metrics join to read again. A copy, a moved checkout or another `--home` registers again.
- After any change to `context/`, `agents/`, or `skills/` reaches this home: the three smoke checks of `TEST-2026-09-03-verify-real-home` on Antigravity, from a fresh clone of the demo service.
- When `govulncheck ./...` names a toolchain-fixed advisory: get a newer Go, never raise the `go` directive or add a `toolchain` line in `go.mod` (ADR-029 — a pin makes the module unbuildable on a host that cannot fetch a toolchain). Try the system package manager first; when it has nothing newer, as Debian trixie did on 2026-09-16 (`golang-1.24-go 1.24.4-1` and no later package), install a user-level SDK instead, which needs no root:

```bash
go install golang.org/dl/go1.27.3@latest     # the wrapper lands in ~/.go/bin
~/.go/bin/go1.27.3 download                  # the SDK lands in ~/sdk/go1.27.3
ln -sfn "$HOME/sdk/go1.27.3/bin/go" "$HOME/.local/bin/go"   # ~/.local/bin is ahead of /usr/local/bin on PATH here
go install golang.org/x/vuln/cmd/govulncheck@latest         # rebuild it, or it cannot parse the newer sources
go version && "$(go env GOPATH)/bin/govulncheck" ./...   # the full path: GOPATH/bin is not on every shell's PATH
```

  Undo by repointing that one symlink at an older SDK under `~/sdk`, or by deleting it: `/usr/bin/go` (go1.24.4) stays where it was; `/usr/local/go`, a root-owned go1.27.1 on 2026-10-09, was gone by 2026-10-26. On 2026-10-09 this box moved to go1.27.2 this way, for GO-2026-6604, -6600 and -6599; on 2026-10-26 to go1.27.3, for GO-2026-6809, after `~/sdk/go1.27.1` had gone missing under the symlink. After the switch, run the full gate and `fyr install`, so the deployed binary is built by the new toolchain — `go version -m ~/.local/bin/fyr` names it.

  The known findings, so a NEW one stands out (moved from the project `AGENTS.md` § Setup commands, 2026-10-29): on go1.27.3, no finding the code reaches (2026-10-26; go1.27.2 reported GO-2026-6809, crypto/x509, not reached). Known in required modules: GO-2026-5024 (golang.org/x/sys via the SQLite driver, not reachable; ADR-045a) and, on a Go before 1.25.12, GO-2026-4970 (os.Root.Open, reached from internal/search, guarded by an Lstat first, and from internal/check, which strips every trailing slash before os.Root sees a name). On a Go older than go1.24.6 or go1.25.8, two standard-library advisories (`os`, `os/exec`): the fix is upgrading the machine's Go, never pinning it.

## Roll back

`fyr uninstall` removes exactly the files the manifest lists, plus the dream timer and `fyr auto`'s timer when installed (leaving `fyr auto`'s config and state), even with no manifest left. To return to an earlier harness commit: `git checkout <commit> && go run ./cmd/fyr install`.

## Sandbox instead of the real home

`TEST-2026-09-03-verify-sandbox` records how a throwaway `HOME` with the CLI logged in is used to test a change end to end before it reaches the real home.

title: Deploy — other machines
body:
# Deploy — other machines

The harness reaches a machine one way: `fyr` (R8, R9, ADR-030, ADR-033); what each kind of place fetches is `SPEC-fyr-delivery` § The model, on the operator's own credentials; there is no push-based deploy, no CI, no hooks, no service.

## First install on a machine

```bash
git clone git@github.com:example-org/fyr.git ~/workspace/fyr
cd ~/workspace/fyr
go run ./cmd/fyr install
fyr status
```

`install` writes only under `~/.gemini/config` and `~/.local/bin` and edits no vendor setting (PRD.md § Non-goals, ADR-062). Check `fyr status` ends with "drift none". A machine that already has `sh-agent` (v2.7.0 or earlier) does not start here: § Crossing to fyr.

On a machine that installs from a RELEASE BINARY instead, the download is verified before it is moved and the install is verified after it — two different checks, and skipping the second is what BUG-078 cost:

```bash
# One chained command: a failed check stops the move. V is the version you expect, from OUTSIDE
# the download (you cut it, or read it on a machine you already trust); ASSET is fyr-linux-amd64,
# fyr-darwin-arm64 or fyr-linux-arm64. macOS: shasum -a 256 -c -
V=vX.Y.Z && ASSET=fyr-linux-amd64 \
&& D=$(mktemp -d) && cd "$D" \
&& gh release download "$V" --repo github.com/example-org/fyr --clobber \
     --pattern "$ASSET" --pattern 'SHA256SUMS' --dir "$D" \
&& grep -qxF "# fyr $V" SHA256SUMS \
&& grep -v '^#' SHA256SUMS | sha256sum -c - --ignore-missing \
&& chmod +x "$ASSET" \
&& test "$("./$ASSET" version)" = "fyr $V" \
&& mv "$ASSET" ~/.local/bin/fyr && cd ~ && rm -r "$D"
# The `grep` and the `test` tie the checksum file and the binary to the version YOU named — what
# `fyr update` does with the tag it asked GitHub for (update also refuses a tag that is not
# newer than what it has, which no first install can mirror). The checksums are not signed
# (ADR-053): they prove the download is whole and is the file the release lists; who made the
# release rests on your GitHub credential and HTTPS. The checksum file leaves with "$D". A system
# path instead of ~/.local/bin is a `sudo mv` on that one line and changes nothing else.

hash -r                               # bash (zsh: rehash): the shell caches where it last found fyr
fyr version                           # unqualified: what the SHELL resolves, after the move
type fyr                              # when the version is wrong: the path the shell actually runs, cached or not
which -a fyr                          # every candidate, in PATH order
```

`fyr version` unqualified is the one that matters, and `hash -r` comes first because a shell caches where it last found `fyr`: `update` replaces `~/.local/bin/fyr` and nothing else, so a shell that once resolved the name to a copy elsewhere keeps running that copy whatever PATH says — example-box stayed on v1.2.1 this way after a successful update to v1.2.2 (BUG-079); `update` now says when it ran from such a copy — but only when the update ran against the real home (never a `--home` elsewhere), and only when the copy it ran from was actually written; the remedy is `ln -sfn` to the installed binary when that copy is yours, or, when it belongs to someone else, removing it with the rights that own it, or leaving it and running the installed one by its path. A binary moved into a system path is not installed if an earlier `PATH` entry holds another `fyr`: that one runs, installs whatever source it resolves, and reports `drift none` about it. It tells stale from fresh, never genuine from forged — it is the suspect binary's own output; what you can check is the checksum on the file, before the move, and it proves integrity only (ADR-053). `install` and `status` name such a binary now (a `warning:` line and a `shadowed` line), and a symlink from the earlier entry to the installed binary settles it — it runs the same file, so it is not a shadow. `--clobber` matters for the same class of reason: without it a leftover file from an earlier attempt makes the download refuse, and the stale file is what gets moved.

The binary is the one file fyr writes through a link. When `~/.local/bin` is a symlink to a directory, `fyr update` on a release-binary place replaces `fyr` in the directory the link points to, while `fyr install` never writes a linked destination or one under a linked directory and prints `keep    ~/<path> (a symlink; fyr never writes through a link)` for it, the binary included. This is accepted, not a defect (audit finding IN39, `PLAN-2026-10-27-audit-choices`): a linked `~/.local/bin` is the operator's own layout, and the binary is the exception to the link rule.

## The four places

The operator installs the harness in four places: the work Mac, the home Mac, and two Linux hosts where they work on other projects; at each the harness serves the Antigravity CLI. Every one is reached on the operator's own SSH key and `gh` login — there are no deploy keys and no per-machine credentials, because the operator authenticates as themselves everywhere and a key would restrict nothing (ADR-030 D1). A place gets the harness one of three ways, named in `SPEC-fyr-delivery` § The model:

- **A checkout the operator owns** — the normal path. First install as above; after that, `fyr update` whenever the operator decides the harness has changed. A timer (§ The resync loop) is a convenience a machine may add, not the mechanism.
- **A release binary** — one downloaded `fyr` with `context/`, `skills/`, `agents/`, `commands/` and `rules/` built into it, for a place that only USES the harness and should not have a checkout of it sitting beside its projects. `fyr install` installs what the binary carries and copies the binary itself; `fyr status` shows `source embedded vX.Y.Z`; `fyr update` downloads the newest release, checks it against its `SHA256SUMS` and replaces `~/.local/bin/fyr` (which place gets what from a tag: `SPEC-fyr-delivery` § The model). `fyr adopt` needs a checkout and says so. See `README.md` § Install without cloning and `DEPLOY-local` § Update a release-binary install.
- **A zip place** — a repository zip downloaded by hand, unpacked and installed with the running binary by `fyr update --from-zip <file>`, which then deletes the unpacked copy; nothing is fetched and nothing in the zip replaces the binary, so the operator moves it forward by repeating the download and `--from-zip`. See `README.md` § Install from a zip (no SSH, no gh).

A plain copy with no `.git` — an unpacked bundle — still installs, and `update` refuses it, naming `install` still deploying it as it is and the alternatives above (`DEPLOY-local` § From a plain copy); it is not one of the ways in, it is the fallback when none of the three can reach GitHub, and it differs from a zip place in what is kept — a plain copy is a tree someone unpacked and left on disk, while a zip place keeps no tree at all.

Nothing else carries the harness: no copy vendored inside a project, no per-project copy, no service. A project that wants the harness installs it with `fyr` into a home. That home receives installed FILES — `fyr install` writes the context, skills, agents, commands and rules and creates no repository. That alone does not stop a change flowing back: changing the harness takes a credential that can push to this repository, not a checkout, and anything that reaches the operator's SSH key or `gh` login can clone and push. A home seeded for agents is therefore read-only only when it reaches no such credential — no forwarded ssh-agent, no `gh` token, no readable key. This repository names no consumer project and depends on none (R8).

Nothing flows back: a place's brain store (every project's trail records and memory, and the global `feedback`, `retro` and `proposal` records), search index and metrics store stay under `~/.config/fyr/` on that place, and a project's memory is `memory` records in that brain store, never a directory in the project (`SPEC-fyr-memory-loop`); the three things that leave a place, all to the model of the CLI it already uses (except a `missing-skill` worker's search of `skills.sh` with the pinned CLI), are the dreamer's redacted prompt, `fyr eval`'s runs (started by the operator or, when `fyr auto` is turned on at level `harness`, by its hourly run), and `fyr work` workers started by the operator or, when `fyr auto` is turned on, by its hourly run (ADR-062, ADR-065, ADR-076, ADR-090; `SPEC-fyr-delivery` § What stays on the machine, `DEPLOY-local` § What stays on this machine).

## Crossing to fyr

What v3.0.0 delivers, and why a place on v2.7.0 or earlier crosses by hand, is `SPEC-fyr-delivery` § The model; this is the procedure, by kind of place. The state-dir migration and the resync below are `fyr install`'s, and run on that first install. The dream timer's replacement under its fyr name was `fyr install`'s too, until every place had crossed (ledger A1, D40); it was removed in ledger Phase 10, and an old-named unit left anywhere is the operator's to remove by hand.

**Before the crossing, at every place.** Disable or rewrite any unit or profile line of the operator's own that names `sh-agent` (on the dev box the hourly `sh-agent-update.timer`: `systemctl --user disable --now sh-agent-update.timer`; it fails today anyway, because the v2.7.0 release binary refuses `--repo`), and rename any exported `SH_AGENT_*` variable to its `FYR_*` name (a set `SH_AGENT_*` variable is not read; the verb prints one stderr notice naming the `FYR_*` name). Do NOT run `sh-agent uninstall` first: it deletes the state the migration carries. Since ledger Phase 10 `fyr install` no longer replaces the old dream timer, so stop and remove it by hand too: `systemctl --user disable --now 'sh-agent-dream*.timer'`, delete `~/.config/systemd/user/sh-agent-dream*.{service,timer}`, then `systemctl --user daemon-reload` (macOS: `launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u) <plist>` for each `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.example.sh-agent-dream*.plist`, then delete it); `fyr dream --install-timer` installs the fyr one.

**A release-binary place.** Run the First install block above with the fyr names (`ASSET=fyr-<os>-<arch>`, `V=v3.0.0`, `# fyr v3.0.0`, `--repo github.com/example-org/fyr`): it checks the marker and the checksum and moves the binary to `~/.local/bin/fyr`. Then `hash -r` and `fyr install`.

**A checkout place.** Stop any own timer that runs `sh-agent update` first. Then:

```bash
git remote set-url origin git@github.com:example-org/fyr.git
git pull --ff-only
go run ./cmd/fyr install --repo "$PWD"
```

`--repo` because a home last installed by a release binary (the dev box runs the v2.7.0 one) refuses a checkout that is only found from the working directory (`knownCheckout`).

**A zip place.** Download the `fyr-<os>-<arch>` asset by hand, as a release-binary place does, verify it the same way and `chmod +x`. Then `./fyr update --from-zip <fyr-v3.0.0.zip>`. A plain-copy install copies the running `./fyr` to `~/.local/bin/fyr`; the zip replaces no binary.

**What `fyr install` does at the crossing.**

- The state dir moves first, before anything opens it, in every verb that writes under it (`install`, `sync`, `update` without `--check` or `--dry-run`, `uninstall`, `adopt`, `index`, `search`, `memory add`, `metrics ingest`, `dream` without `--dry-run`). With `~/.config/fyr` absent and `~/.config/sh-agent` a plain directory, one `os.Rename` moves it and the verb prints `migrated ~/.config/sh-agent → ~/.config/fyr`. With both present neither is touched: one line says `fyr` reads `~/.config/fyr` and leaves `~/.config/sh-agent` for the operator to merge or remove. With `~/.config/sh-agent` a symlink (and `~/.config/fyr` absent) the verb is refused: move what it points to to `~/.config/fyr` (or point a `~/.config/fyr` link at it) and run again.
- Read-only verbs and modes never migrate (`status`, `diff`, `list`, `render`, `version`, `memory show`, `metrics show|report|evals|export`, every `--dry-run`, `update --check`): with the old dir present they print one stderr line, `run fyr install to migrate ~/.config/sh-agent`, and read nothing from it.
- The resync reads the old manifest from the moved dir. Claude Code's files from that install (`~/.claude/AGENTS.md`, the `CLAUDE.md` stub, `~/.claude/{agents,skills,commands,rules}/*`) stay exactly as they are: they leave fyr's manifest, install says so in one line (`keep    ~/.claude: <n> files an install before fyr wrote for Claude Code; fyr never removes them, and they leave its manifest`), and no later `fyr install` or `fyr uninstall` touches them (plan `2026-10-24-fyr-agy-only.md` D32: a Claude Code still used on a machine keeps its files, frozen at v2.7.0's text). Every other file the old manifest lists and the new plan does not — `~/.local/bin/sh-agent` — is removed. A symlink, or a path under a linked directory, stays (the operator's). A removal error stops the install: remove the file by hand and run `fyr install` again. `~/.claude/settings.json` stays too; the two keys v2.7.0 wrote there (`attribution`, `autoCompactWindow`) are the operator's to keep or remove.
- `fyr status` names every `sh-agent` PATH finds with a `leftover` line (F4).

**After the crossing, at every place:**

```bash
hash -r
fyr version                                   # fyr v3.0.0 or newer
fyr status                                    # no warning, ends "drift none"
ls ~/.config/sh-agent ~/.local/bin/sh-agent   # both: No such file or directory
systemctl --user list-timers | grep -cw sh-agent   # 0 (macOS: launchctl list | grep -cw sh-agent)
```

**Accepted risks after the crossing.**

- A Claude Code session at a crossed place still runs the v2.7.0 harness under `~/.claude`, which fyr keeps frozen (above), and that harness's `feedback-log` writes under `~/.config/sh-agent`, bringing the old directory back (it did on the dev box on 2026-10-26, `TEST-2026-10-26-2233-verify-the-crossing-to-fyr-at-the-work-mac-the-h`). With both directories present no verb moves anything: each prints the both-directories notice and fyr reads only `~/.config/fyr`. Merge or remove the old directory by hand, and stop using Claude Code there, or remove its v2.7.0 files, to end it.
- The crossings of the work Mac, the home Mac and the second Linux host rest on the operator's word ("Crossed, all clean", the same testing record): no `fyr status` line or binary version from those places is recorded. Only the dev box's crossing was checked by commands (`TEST-2026-10-26-2217-verify-the-crossing-to-fyr-on-the-dev-box-and-th`).

## The resync loop

```bash
# machine A: change, verify, install, commit, push
fyr install && git add <the file> && git commit -m "context: tweak" && git push
# machine B
fyr update            # fetch; refuse a dirty checkout; if behind: pull --ff-only; rebuild and reinstall
fyr update --check    # only reports; exit 2 when behind, 0 when current; on a dirty checkout it prints the real run's refusal and exits 1 (so does --dry-run)
```

`fyr update` finds the checkout from `$FYR_REPO`, then the working directory or any of its parents, then the path recorded at the last install, so it works from anywhere. It refuses a non-fast-forward pull; resolve that by hand in the checkout.

**`update` refuses a checkout with uncommitted changes, whether or not it is behind.** It deploys the WORKING TREE, not the commit it just fetched, so on a machine where the harness is also being edited it would put half-finished work into the live context — which is what an hourly timer did here on 2026-09-16 (BUG-046). Commit or stash, or run `fyr install` to deploy a dirty tree deliberately. That makes `update` safe to run from a timer:

```ini
# ~/.config/systemd/user/fyr-update.service  — with the matching hourly .timer
[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=%h/.local/bin/fyr update --repo %h/workspace/fyr
Environment=PATH=%h/.local/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin
```

The dev box's old `sh-agent-update` unit is disabled at its crossing (§ Crossing to fyr), not carried over.

On a box where nobody edits the checkout the timer simply keeps it current; on a box where somebody does, it now declines instead of deploying their draft.

The timer follows `main` by fast-forward: its trust root is whoever can push to this repository, exactly as a hand-typed `fyr update` is. That is the operator, on their own machines, and the accepted position (ADR-030). A box where that is not acceptable runs `fyr update --check` on the timer and updates by hand (on a dirty checkout that run exits 1 with the refusal, not 2). What a tag delivers, and to which place: `SPEC-fyr-delivery` § The model.

## Releases — tags, as release markers

A release is an annotated `vX.Y.Z` tag on `main`, and the binaries published with it, with their `SHA256SUMS`. No key signs anything (ADR-053, superseding ADR-026's signing, ADR-033's signed checksums and ADR-052). What a tag delivers, and to which kind of place, is `SPEC-fyr-delivery` § The model (ADR-033, superseding ADR-030 D2; the history of the channel is there too). v3.0.0 is a MAJOR because the installed command changes name; its notes carry § Crossing to fyr. A release is cut by `/preflight vX.Y.Z` from the operator's own turn, from this checkout (never a plain copy), on any machine where the operator is logged in to GitHub (`gh auth status`). Nothing else is tagged: no lightweight tag, no `-rc` suffix, no other prefix. Only a canonical `vX.Y.Z` (no leading zeros, e.g. never `v1.02.2`) counts as a release tag anywhere in this repository's tooling, so never cut one with a leading zero — every place refuses it. The tag is the only version tracking; there is no version file.

Procedure — what `/preflight` runs at its Step 6 here (the skill's Step 6.3 follows a project's Release section), each command its own call, its exit status read before the next; `<gated head>` is the head SHA of the gate report's `Range reviewed:` line, the one external input — the tag itself takes no target, so no placeholder can sit on both sides of a check:
```bash
gh auth status                                                                                          # exit 0: this machine can push and publish
# gate passed and the release commit made (preflight Step 6.3): HEAD is that commit; <gated head> is the head SHA of the gate report's `Range reviewed:` line
go test -count=1 -run TestDeliverySpecCurrent ./cmd/fyr                                                # exit 0: the release's `change` record (ID …-release-vX-Y-Z) and `SPEC-fyr-delivery` § Where things stand both name vX.Y.Z (BUG-167)
test -z "$(git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all)"                                              # exit 0: clean tree — the bare form inherits status.showUntrackedFiles (BUG-049)
# BEFORE the tag, never after the push: `go:embed` reads the WORKING TREE, so a stray file under the
# five embedded directories is compiled into every released binary. The clean-tree test above cannot
# see an IGNORED file, and a tag is unrecallable once pushed (D23, BUG-066; security review 2026-09-17)
test -z "$(git status --porcelain --ignored --untracked-files=all -- context skills agents commands rules)"   # exit 0: nothing untracked or ignored there
go test -count=1 -run TestEmbedHoldsOnlyTrackedFiles ./...                                             # exit 0: the embedded set is exactly what git tracks
test "$(git rev-parse HEAD^)" = "$(git rev-parse <gated head>)"                                        # exit 0: the release commit sits on the gated head
git diff --quiet <gated head> HEAD -- ':(top)' ':(top,exclude).agents/trail.jsonl'                      # exit 0: records only — ':(top)' because a bare '.' is relative to the cwd and misses a change in a sibling directory (measured)
git tag -a vX.Y.Z -m "fyr vX.Y.Z"                                                                     # no target argument: tags HEAD
# check the tag before any push — every line carries its verdict in its exit status:
test "$(git rev-parse vX.Y.Z^{commit})" = "$(git rev-parse HEAD)"                                      # exit 0: the tag is on the release commit
git merge-base --is-ancestor vX.Y.Z^{commit} main                                                       # exit 0: on main
test "$(git cat-file -t vX.Y.Z)" = tag                                                                  # exit 0: annotated ("commit" means lightweight)
git push origin main
git push origin vX.Y.Z                                                                                  # plain pushes, never --force
```

Then the release's binaries (`SPEC-fyr-delivery` § The model; R9, ADR-033). Built here, from the tagged tree, never by a service:
```bash
# 0. the contamination guard AGAIN, here: it ran before the tag so a bad tree is
#    never tagged, and it runs again here because `go:embed` reads the working
#    tree at BUILD time — which is after the tag and the pushes, so a .DS_Store
#    or an editor swap file appearing under skills/ in between would otherwise be
#    embedded unguarded (D23, BUG-066; code review 2026-09-17 round 2). Both
#    commands are read-only, so running them twice costs nothing.
test -z "$(git status --porcelain --ignored --untracked-files=all -- context skills agents commands rules)"   # exit 0: nothing untracked or ignored there
go test -count=1 -run TestEmbedHoldsOnlyTrackedFiles ./...                 # exit 0: embedded set == git's
# 1. the three platforms, from the tag's own tree, reproducible flags
for target in linux/amd64 darwin/arm64 linux/arm64; do
  GOOS="${target%/*}" GOARCH="${target#*/}" CGO_ENABLED=0 GOTOOLCHAIN=local \
    go build -trimpath -ldflags "-X main.version=vX.Y.Z" \
    -o ".agents/scratch/release-vX.Y.Z/fyr-${target%/*}-${target#*/}" ./cmd/fyr
done
# 1b. the zip of the tagged tree, for a zip place (ADR-039): `update --from-zip` checks it
#    against this release's SHA256SUMS when that sits beside it
git archive --format=zip --prefix=fyr-vX.Y.Z/ -o .agents/scratch/release-vX.Y.Z/fyr-vX.Y.Z.zip vX.Y.Z
# 2. the checksums, with the VERSION as the first line — `fyr update` refuses a
#    release whose SHA256SUMS names another version or none (D26 of the
#    release-binary plan), and `sha256sum -c` ignores a '#' line
cd .agents/scratch/release-vX.Y.Z
printf '# fyr %s\n' vX.Y.Z > SHA256SUMS
if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  sha256sum fyr-linux-amd64 fyr-darwin-arm64 fyr-linux-arm64 fyr-vX.Y.Z.zip >> SHA256SUMS
  sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS                                                  # exit 0: the file describes these files
else
  shasum -a 256 fyr-linux-amd64 fyr-darwin-arm64 fyr-linux-arm64 fyr-vX.Y.Z.zip >> SHA256SUMS
  grep -v '^#' SHA256SUMS | shasum -a 256 -c -                             # exit 0 on macOS without GNU coreutils
fi
# 3. BEFORE anything is published: this host's own built binary checks the release zip
#    against SHA256SUMS, as a zip place will (ADR-039)
mkdir -p ../zipcheck && "./fyr-$(go env GOOS)-$(go env GOARCH)" update --from-zip fyr-vX.Y.Z.zip --home ../zipcheck --dry-run > ../zipcheck.out   # into a file, never a pipe (BUG-086)
grep -q "CHECKED against the SHA256SUMS of release vX.Y.Z" ../zipcheck.out   # exit 0
# 4. the release, with notes read by the operator before the upload — created with the
#    notes ALONE, then one upload per asset: a create carrying every asset rolls the whole
#    release back when a single upload fails, which is what GitHub did twice for v1.1.0
#    (`HTTP 500: Error creating asset temp dir`), while one call per file then worked first
#    time each. Retry an individual upload before calling it a failure.
gh release create vX.Y.Z --repo github.com/example-org/fyr --verify-tag --title "fyr vX.Y.Z" \
  --notes-file ../release-notes-vX.Y.Z.md
for a in SHA256SUMS fyr-linux-amd64 fyr-darwin-arm64 fyr-linux-arm64 fyr-vX.Y.Z.zip; do
  gh release upload vX.Y.Z --repo github.com/example-org/fyr "$a" --clobber || echo "retry $a by hand"
done
gh release view vX.Y.Z --repo github.com/example-org/fyr --json assets --jq '.assets[].name'   # all five
cd -
```

The release notes are built as § Release notes below says. Before this repository is ever made public, read the trail for what it names (this box's login-shell credential broker, `/etc/profile.d/zz-example-credentials.sh`, is described in `BUG-160` § Addendum and the 2026-10-07 security reviews under `reviews/`): the trail, `.agents/trail.jsonl`, carries hostnames (`example-mac.example.invalid`, `example-box`), machine paths (`/opt/example/deploy/harness`), links to the operator's private web artifacts (the "Harness Delivery Map" page, in the 2026-10-09 handoff and changes entry), and a report record's contents, all of which are fine inside a private repository and are internal identifiers outside one. There is no secret in them — that is checked every release — but publication is a separate decision from releasing, and this is the paragraph that says so (security review 2026-09-18).
