title: Research — hooks for the harness (2026-09-03)
body:
# Research — hooks for the harness   (2026-09-03)

## Question

The operator may want hooks after all: (1) a deploy gate that verifies everything is documented and up to date, (2) a warning when the wrong model is in use, (3) a loop protector. What do Claude Code and the Antigravity CLI actually offer, what would each hook look like on both, what does it cost, and what is worth building?

Constraints that shape the answer: zero scripts in the repo (any hook is a subcommand of the `sh-agent` binary), no CI, both vendors served alike, and the previous harness's hooks were reverted because a wrong block cost eight forced continuations and a degraded agent (old ADR-002, R4). Whatever is built must fail open and block only at a boundary the operator would block at by hand.

## Summary

Both CLIs have a `PreToolUse` hook that can deny, ask, or allow a tool call from a JSON payload on stdin, and a `Stop` hook that can refuse a stop. That is enough for all three wishes. Claude Code additionally exposes the model to hooks (`SessionStart` sometimes, `PostModelSwitch` always) and has an `if` filter so a hook only spawns for matching commands; Antigravity puts `modelName` in every payload and has `PreInvocation` for injecting a message before each model call. Neither has built-in repeated-call detection.

Recommendation, in order of value: build the **loop protector** and the **model warning** (small, deterministic, session-wide), and build the **deploy gate as "a fresh `/preflight` SHIP report for HEAD must exist"** rather than as a hook that judges documentation itself — a hook can check that the check happened; only the `preflight` skill and the `documentation` agent can check content. Do **not** build a Stop-hook that blocks until docs are written: that is the design that was reverted. All three are subcommands of `sh-agent` (`sh-agent hook <name>`), so the repo stays at zero scripts. The one real cost is that Claude Code hooks live in `~/.claude/settings.json`, so the installer would have to add and remove a `hooks` block there — the operator has said no settings changes before; this is the decision to make.

## What each vendor offers

| | Claude Code | Antigravity CLI (agy 1.1.24) |
|---|---|---|
| Config location | `~/.claude/settings.json` (user), `.claude/settings.json` / `.claude/settings.local.json` (project), plugin `hooks/hooks.json`, subagent frontmatter `hooks:` (scoped to that agent), skill frontmatter `hooks:` (registered when the skill is invoked, kept for the session) | one `hooks.json` in the customization root: `~/.gemini/config/hooks.json` (global) or `.agents/hooks.json` (workspace); named hooks, merged by name; `"enabled": false` per hook |
| Events | `SessionStart`, `SessionEnd`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `PostToolUseFailure`, `PostToolBatch`, `PermissionRequest`, `PermissionDenied`, `Stop`, `StopFailure`, `SubagentStart`, `SubagentStop`, `PreModelSwitch`, `PostModelSwitch`, `PreCompact`, `PostCompact`, `Notification`, `FileChanged`, `CwdChanged`, and more | `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `PreInvocation` (before each model call), `PostInvocation` (after tool calls finish), `Stop` |
| Matcher | tool name, `A\|B`, regex; plus `if: "Bash(git push *)"` in permission-rule syntax so the hook only spawns for matching arguments | tool name regex on `PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse` (`run_command`, `browser_.*`, `*`) |
| Input (stdin JSON) | `session_id`, `transcript_path`, `cwd`, `permission_mode`, `hook_event_name`; `PreToolUse`: `tool_name`, `tool_input`, `tool_use_id`, `effort.level`; `Stop`: `stop_hook_active`, `last_assistant_message`; `SessionStart`: `reason`, `model` (not always); `PostModelSwitch`: the model | common: `conversationId`, `workspacePaths`, `transcriptPath`, `artifactDirectoryPath`, **`modelName`**; `PreToolUse`: `toolCall{name,args{CommandLine…}}`, `stepIdx`; `PostToolUse`: `error`; `PreInvocation`: `invocationNum`, `initialNumSteps`; `Stop`: `executionNum`, `terminationReason` (`model_stop`, `max_steps_exceeded`, `error`), `fullyIdle` |
| Output | exit 0 = continue (stdout becomes context for `SessionStart`/`UserPromptSubmit`); exit 2 + stderr = block; or JSON: `hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision` allow/deny/ask/defer, `permissionDecisionReason`, `additionalContext`, `updatedInput`; `decision: "block"` + `reason` on `Stop`/`PostToolUse`; `systemMessage` | JSON only: `PreToolUse` → `decision` allow/deny/ask/force_ask, `reason`, `overwrite`; `PostToolUse` → `{}`; `PreInvocation`/`PostInvocation` → `injectSteps[{ephemeralMessage\|userMessage\|toolCall}]`, `terminationBehavior` force_continue/terminate; `Stop` → `decision: "continue"` + `reason` |
| Hook types | `command`, `http`, `mcp_tool`, `prompt` (a model judges), `agent` | `command` only |
| Timeout | per hook; defaults 10 min for commands, 30 s for prompt-submit/model-switch | per hook, default 30 s; hooks run synchronously |
| Working dir / command | runs with the session cwd | runs in the directory holding `hooks.json`, via `sh -c`, `~` expanded — so the command must be `~/.local/bin/sh-agent …` or on PATH |
| Built-in loop limits | subagent `maxTurns`; `/goal` evaluator; `stop_hook_active` so a Stop hook is not re-invoked forever | `max_steps_exceeded` termination; 60 s default subagent interaction timeout |
| Model control | `model`, `enforceAvailableModels`, `fallbackModel` in settings; `PreModelSwitch` hook can deny a switch; status line JSON has `model.id`/`display_name` | `--model` flag; `modelName` in every hook payload (`auto` when not pinned) |

Sources: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide.md, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents.md, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.md, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference.md, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline.md, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal.md; the "Lifecycle Hooks (`hooks.json`)" guide embedded in the agy binary and `agy changelog`.

## The three hooks, designed for both vendors

All three are `sh-agent hook <name>` subcommands reading stdin JSON and printing the vendor's JSON. Vendor is detected from the payload (`hook_event_name` vs `conversationId`). Every hook fails open: any error, unknown payload, or timeout means "allow, say nothing".

### 1. Deploy gate — "everything documented and up to date"

**What a hook can and cannot decide.** Whether the README, spec, and changelog *match the code* is a judgement; a hook can only check facts on disk. The facts worth checking before a deploy: the tree is clean, HEAD is what will be deployed, and a release gate has run on exactly this HEAD. `/preflight` already does the judgement part (docs freshness via the `documentation` agent, trail freshness, tests, review) and writes `reviews/<date>-preflight-*.md` with `Range reviewed: <base>..<head>` and `VERDICT: SHIP`. So:

- **Trigger:** Claude `PreToolUse`, `matcher: Bash`, `if: Bash(gcloud run deploy *)` plus `Bash(gcloud run services update *)`, `Bash(docker push *)`, `Bash(terraform apply *)`, `Bash(kubectl apply *)`; Antigravity `PreToolUse` on `run_command`, the same regexes applied to `args.CommandLine` inside the hook.
- **Check:** `git status --porcelain` empty; newest `.agents/docs/reviews/*-preflight-*.md` has a `Range reviewed:` line ending in the current `HEAD` short SHA and a `VERDICT: SHIP` line. A `docker push` to `pkg.dev` also requires the image tag to equal the HEAD short SHA when the tag is visible in the command.
- **Result:** pass → allow silently. Fail → `ask` (Claude `permissionDecision: ask`, agy `decision: ask`) with the reason ("no preflight report for HEAD a1b2c3d — run /preflight, or approve to deploy anyway"). Ask, not deny: the operator stays in control, and a deliberate hot-fix deploy costs one keypress instead of a fight.
- **Not gated:** `git push`. Git is backup; a gate on push blocks backups.
- **Cost:** one git call and one directory scan per deploy command; the hook does not spawn for other commands on Claude (the `if` filter), and costs a few milliseconds per command on agy.

Alternative considered and rejected: a `Stop` hook that blocks until a changelog entry exists. It fires every turn, it is wrong whenever the turn was not the end of a task, and it is the exact mechanism that was reverted. A softer variant — `Stop` hook that only *warns* ("source changed since HEAD, no changes/ entry today") via `systemMessage`, never blocks — is cheap and could be added later if the prose Definition of Done is being ignored.

### 2. Wrong-model warning

- **Claude:** `SessionStart` (payload `model` when present) and `PostModelSwitch` (always). If the model id is not in the allowed list, print one line to stdout (exit 0 → it lands in context) and set `systemMessage` so the operator sees it: "Model is claude-haiku-4-5; expected claude-fable-5-1 or claude-opus-5". Optionally `PreModelSwitch` with `permissionDecision: ask` to confirm a switch to a model outside the list. No blocking.
- **Antigravity:** `PreInvocation` fires before every model call and carries `modelName`. On `invocationNum == 1` only, if `modelName` is not allowed (or is `auto` when a pin is required), inject `{"ephemeralMessage": "…"}`; nothing on later invocations.
- **Allowed list:** given as arguments in the hook config itself (`sh-agent hook model --allow claude-fable-5-1,claude-opus-5` / `--allow pro`), so there is no extra config file; the installer templates the lists from one place in the repo (`context/` or a small `hooks/` directory the installer reads).
- **Cheaper alternative on Claude:** no hook; pin `model` in `~/.claude/settings.json` (already done: `claude-fable-5-1[1m]`) and read the status line. The hook only adds value if sessions get started with `--model` or switched with `/model`.

### 3. Loop protector

- **Signal:** the same tool call (tool name + argument hash) repeated three times in a row **with no file-changing call in between**. The "no edit in between" rule removes the common false positive: running `go test ./...` three times is fine when an `Edit` sits between the runs. `PostToolUse` records the result hash as well; identical input and identical output twice in a row is a loop by definition.
- **Claude:** `PreToolUse` on every tool (`matcher: ""`) reads `session_id`, `tool_name`, `tool_input`; `PostToolUse` appends the result hash. State is one small file per session under the CLI's own temp dir (`$TMPDIR/sh-agent/<session_id>`), so nothing persists. On a loop: `permissionDecision: ask`, reason "same call for the 3rd time with no change in between — loop?". `Stop` is left alone (no Stop hook), so no risk of the forced-continuation spiral.
- **Antigravity:** `PreToolUse` on `*` with `toolCall.name` + `args` hash keyed by `conversationId`; `PostToolUse` has no result body, so only the input rule applies. On a loop: `decision: ask` with the reason. `PostInvocation` could add `terminationBehavior: terminate` when `invocationNum` passes a hard ceiling with no edits since, as a second line of defence.
- **Subagents:** already capped by `maxTurns` (20–40) in `agents/*.md`; the hook applies to them too on Claude.
- **Cost:** one hash and one small file append per tool call, a few milliseconds. No model calls.

## What it would take

| Piece | Where | Size |
|---|---|---|
| `sh-agent hook deploy-gate\|model\|loop` | `internal/hook/` + `cmd/sh-agent` | ~350 lines Go incl. vendor payload detection, plus tests against recorded payloads |
| Claude config | `hooks` block in `~/.claude/settings.json`; installer merges by our command prefix (`~/.local/bin/sh-agent hook`) and removes only those entries on uninstall | ~80 lines Go; the one settings write the harness has avoided so far |
| Antigravity config | named entries `sh-agent-deploy`, `sh-agent-model`, `sh-agent-loop` in `~/.gemini/config/hooks.json`; installer merges by name | ~40 lines Go |
| Repo source of truth | `hooks/` directory with one JSON per hook in a vendor-neutral shape (event, matcher/if, command args) that the installer renders into both formats — so a new hook is a file, not code, once the subcommand exists | small |
| Docs | README, `context/AGENTS.md` (the gate's "run /preflight first"), ADR | small |

Option B for Claude that avoids the global settings write: `/init-project` writes the hooks into the project's `.claude/settings.json`. Per project, versioned with the project, but every project must be initialised for the hooks to exist, and the model warning would not fire outside a project.

Option C: skill-scoped hooks. `cloud-run-deploy` and `preflight` could carry the deploy gate in their SKILL.md `hooks:` frontmatter, active for the session once the skill is invoked. No settings write at all, but the gate exists only after the skill was loaded — an agent that runs `gcloud run deploy` without loading the skill is not gated. Fine as a belt when the braces exist, not on its own.

## Risks

- A hook that misparses a payload and denies is worse than no hook. Hence ask-not-deny everywhere, fail-open, and payload fixtures in tests.
- Claude's `if` syntax and hook payload fields have changed across versions; the `model` field on `SessionStart` is documented as "not always present". Pin what the code expects and test against fixtures recorded from the installed version.
- Antigravity hooks run synchronously with a 30 s default timeout; a slow git repo could stall a `run_command`. Keep the deploy gate to `git status` and a directory scan.
- The loop protector's state file must be per session and cleaned by the OS temp dir; never write it into the repo.
- None of this is verified live on either CLI yet; the live check of the base harness comes first.

## Open questions for the operator

1. Build all three, or only the loop protector and the model warning?
2. Is a merged `hooks` block in `~/.claude/settings.json` acceptable (installer-managed, removed on uninstall), or per-project via `/init-project` (Option B)?
3. Deploy gate: `ask` (recommended) or hard `deny`?
4. Allowed models: Claude `claude-fable-5-1`, `claude-opus-5`? Antigravity `pro` only, or is `auto` fine?
5. Loop threshold: 3 identical calls with no edit in between (recommended), or stricter?

## Decision (2026-09-03)

Rejected by the operator: "Skip the hooks. I think this was my problem before. Keep the no hooks/scripts rule." Recorded as ADR-007. This document stays as the record of what was considered.

title: Plan — a signed release zip that `--from-zip` verifies (2026-09-28)
body:
# Plan — a signed release zip that `--from-zip` verifies   (2026-09-28)

## Why

The v1.8.0 gate's open medium: an unsigned zip becomes the agents' instructions, and `UNVERIFIED` only discloses that (`reviews/2026-09-28-preflight-v1.8.0.md` row 1). The handoff put the fix to the operator as Next Steps 1b: "/preflight could publish a `git archive` zip under the signed SHA256SUMS, and --from-zip would verify it … changes R9's Release procedure, so it needs your approval". The operator answered, 2026-09-28: "All approved. Cut new version if needed. All needs to be fixed."

## Scope

- **In:**
  - Each release publishes `example-harness-vX.Y.Z.zip`, a `git archive` of the tag with the top folder `example-harness-vX.Y.Z/`, listed in the signed `SHA256SUMS`.
  - `update --from-zip` verifies a zip when `SHA256SUMS` and `SHA256SUMS.sig` sit in the same directory as the zip. Otherwise it installs the zip marked `UNVERIFIED`, as today.
  - REQUIREMENTS R9 (the Release bullet and the zip place), ADR-039, the release procedure (`deploy/remote.md` § Releases), README, and `delivery.md`.
- **Out:**
  - a new flag;
  - verifying a `main` zip, which has no signature to check;
  - a manifest change.
- **Follow-ups, not built:** a zip handed over WITHOUT its sums still installs, marked UNVERIFIED, as R9 allows. This change narrows the v1.8.0 medium rather than closing it. Requiring an explicit `--unverified` would be a REQUIREMENTS R9 change and is put to the operator (ADR-039 Open; security reviews r1–r2).

## Surfaces touched

- `internal/harness/release.go`: `verifyRelease` (lines 219-294) splits into `verifySignedSums(keygen, sumsDir, signersDir) (sums []byte, tag string, err error)` and the per-asset check. `verifyRelease` keeps its behaviour and error texts; the existing `TestUpdateFromRelease*` tests pin them.
- `internal/harness/zip.go`: `UnpackZip` gains a check that runs after hashing and before anything is written.
- `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` (`updateFromZip`); tests in `internal/harness/zip_test.go` and `cmd/sh-agent/zip_test.go`.
- `REQUIREMENTS.md` R9; `.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md` ADR-039; `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md` § Releases (the build, checksum and upload lines, and "all five" becoming six); `README.md` § Install from a zip; `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/delivery.md` § The model.

## Interfaces

- **`func UnpackZip(zipPath, parent string, check func(sum string) error) (dir, sum string, err error)`.** `check` may be nil. It runs once, right after the sha256 of the one read buffer is known, before `zip.NewReader`, and its error is returned unchanged, with nothing written.
- **`func VerifyZipSums(zipPath, sum string) (tag string, err error)`**, with `ErrZipUnsigned` beside it, in `internal/harness/release.go` next to `verifySignedSums` and `checksumFor`.
  - It looks for `SHA256SUMS` and `SHA256SUMS.sig` in `filepath.Dir(zipPath)`.
  - Neither present: it returns `"", ErrZipUnsigned`, a new sentinel.
  - Only one present: an error naming the missing one.
  - Both present:
    1. It writes the compiled-in signer to a temp directory, `os.MkdirTemp("", "sh-agent-verify-*")`, removed in a `defer`.
    2. `verifySignedSums` checks the signature and reads the `# example-harness vX.Y.Z` marker.
    3. `checksumFor(sums, filepath.Base(zipPath))` must equal `sum`.

    Any failure is an error, and the zip is refused.
  - It returns the marker's tag.
- **`updateFromZip`** passes a `check` closure that calls `VerifyZipSums` and handles `ErrZipUnsigned` ITSELF (D3):
  - `ErrZipUnsigned`: the closure records "unverified" and returns nil, so `UnpackZip` goes on to unpack, and the output says `UNVERIFIED` as today;
  - success: the closure records the tag and returns nil, and the first line reads `zip <file> (sha256 <hex>, VERIFIED against the signed SHA256SUMS of release vX.Y.Z)`, and the rest is unchanged;
  - any other error: the closure returns it, `UnpackZip` returns it unchanged with nothing written, and the command exits non-zero.
- **The release asset:** `git archive --format=zip --prefix=example-harness-vX.Y.Z/ -o <release dir>/example-harness-vX.Y.Z.zip vX.Y.Z`, added to the `sha256sum` line and the upload loop in `deploy/remote.md` § Releases.
- **REQUIREMENTS R9.**
  - The Release bullet: "…and publishes that tag's binaries with checksums signed by the same key." becomes "…and publishes that tag's binaries and a zip of its tree (`git archive`), with checksums signed by the same key."
  - The zip place sub-bullet gains: "When the release's `SHA256SUMS` and `SHA256SUMS.sig` sit beside the zip, the zip is verified against them and refused if either check fails; a zip without them is installed marked `UNVERIFIED`."
  - The approval note records "All approved", 2026-09-28, and ADR-039.

## Failure modes

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| The `.sig` is missing, or only one of the two files is there | Refused, naming the missing file |
| The signature is bad, or a different key signed it | Refused: "SHA256SUMS signature does not verify (…)" |
| The zip is renamed (a browser's `(1)` suffix), so `SHA256SUMS` has no line for it | Refused: "no line names <file>", with a hint to use the release's file name |
| The checksum differs | Refused: "checksum mismatch" |
| `ssh-keygen` is missing | Refused: "ssh-keygen not found; cannot verify" |

In every case the verification runs before any write, so the home is untouched.

## Verification

- **Unit tests** (`internal/harness`, with `newRelease`'s key and a zip built by `writeZip`):
  - verified;
  - `.sig` missing;
  - a foreign key;
  - checksum mismatch;
  - renamed zip;
  - no sums (`ErrZipUnsigned`);
  - `check`'s error stops the unpack before any write.
- **The existing `TestUpdateFromRelease*`** tests stay green unchanged.
- **CLI:** `cmd/sh-agent`, isolated with an empty `PATH` except `ssh-keygen`, linked into a temp bin the way the release tests do. A verified zip prints `VERIFIED` and installs; a tampered checksum refuses and leaves the home empty.
- **E2E criterion:** a release-versioned build verifies a `git archive` zip of `HEAD`, signed with a scratch key in the release layout, and prints `VERIFIED`. Flipping one byte of the zip refuses it with nothing written. The real v1.9.0 zip is verified the same way after the release, with the real key (operator smoke).

## Phases

- [x] Cold-reader check — r1 needed revision (fixed as D3); r2 was implementation ready with zero BLOCKING questions, and its non-blocking points are D4–D7 (`reviews/2026-09-28-coldread-signed-zip-r{1,2}.md`)
### Phase 1 — Verification and CLI
- [x] Refactor `verifyRelease` → `verifySignedSums` — verify: `go test -race -run 'TestUpdateFromRelease|TestVerifier' ./internal/harness`, AI — expect: pass unchanged
- [x] `UnpackZip` check hook and `VerifyZipSums` — verify: `go test -race -run 'TestVerifyZipSums|TestUnpackZipCheck' ./internal/harness`, AI — expect: the unit cases above, each seen red first
- [x] `updateFromZip` wiring and output — verify: `go test -race -run 'TestUpdateFromZipVerified|TestUpdateFromZipTampered' ./cmd/sh-agent`, AI — expect: `VERIFIED` printed; a tampered zip refused with an empty home
- [x] Checkpoint — expect: full suite green — evidence: `testing/2026-09-28-verify-signed-zip.md` PASS, 2026-09-28
### Phase 2 — Requirements, ADR, release procedure, docs, E2E, one commit
- [x] R9 text, ADR-039, `deploy/remote.md` § Releases, README, `delivery.md` — docs: those files — verify: `/review --docs` — expect: no stale "unsigned only" statement
- [x] E2E criterion — verify: the scratch-key run, AI
- [x] `reviewer` and `security` over the diff; `verifier` — expect: findings fixed or rebutted
- [x] Checkpoint — expect: one commit, pushed — evidence: the signed-zip commit on `main` (`git log --grep 'signed release zip'`), 2026-09-28

## Risks

Assumptions: none open. `git archive` keeps the tracked symlink `.agents/skills`, which sits outside the five trees, so `checkZipTrees` never opens it (`internal/harness/zip.go`); a symlink inside the five trees is refused. Both are covered by the zip plan's tests.

## Decisions

- D1 — 2026-09-28 — The check hook sits inside `UnpackZip`, so the sum is taken from the same buffer that is unpacked (security review r1, low 3) and verification precedes every write — by: implementer.
- D2 — 2026-09-28 — The sums are found beside the zip, with no flag. The operator downloads three files from the Releases page into one folder — by: implementer.
- D3 — 2026-09-28 — `UnpackZip`'s hook stays one rule (any error refuses, nothing written). The unsigned case is not an error at that level: `updateFromZip`'s closure turns `ErrZipUnsigned` into "unverified" and returns nil. One read, one buffer — by: cold read round 1 (`reviews/2026-09-28-coldread-signed-zip-r1.md`, finding 1).
- D4 — 2026-09-28 — The closure reports back through variables it captures in `updateFromZip` (`verifiedTag string`) — by: implementer, cold read r2.
- D5 — 2026-09-28 — `verifySignedSums` returns the marker's tag, and `verifyRelease` compares it with the tag it expects, keeping its existing error text — by: implementer, cold read r2.
- D6 — 2026-09-28 — No separate check of the file name against the tag: `checksumFor(sums, base(zip))` already requires that exact name in the signed file, so a renamed or foreign zip is refused — by: implementer, cold read r1–r2.
- D7 — 2026-09-28 — `SHA256SUMS` and its `.sig` found beside a zip that does not match them refuse it, rather than degrading to UNVERIFIED. Signed sums in the zip's folder say it is meant to be a release zip, so a mismatch is the case to stop at. The error names the release the sums belong to, and never suggests removing them (security review r1, finding 2: that hint was a one-step bypass) — by: implementer, cold read r2; amended after security r1.
- Rejected:
  - a `--sums` flag, one more thing to type wrong;
  - refusing every unsigned zip, which would break the approved `main` zip path (R9).

title: Plan — `sh-agent update --from-zip <file>` (2026-09-28)
body:
# Plan — `sh-agent update --from-zip <file>`   (2026-09-28)

## Why

A machine that can neither hold the operator's SSH key nor run `gh`, such as a corporate workstation, cannot reach the harness today. A checkout needs git over SSH, and `sh-agent update` on a release binary downloads through `gh` (R8, R9). The operator can download the repository zip by hand in a browser.

The operator's words, 2026-09-28:
- "add the --from-zip option so i can run manually";
- then "approve as written, go all but number 6".

That approval covers the REQUIREMENTS text quoted under Interfaces, scope items 1–5 and 7, and, for item 7, the recommended matrix option 1. Item 6 is out: the pasted proposal's report stripping, `trigger: always_on` frontmatter, Cloudtop overlay and skill filtering.

Recon: `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-28-recon-from-zip.md`.

## Scope

- **In:**
  - `sh-agent update --from-zip <file>` from any binary, release or development build (D7 says what other commands do afterwards). It unpacks the zip into a temporary directory under `~/.config/sh-agent/`, refuses any entry that would leave it, installs that tree with the running binary (no rebuild, no binary replacement), and deletes the directory.
  - The manifest marks the install as coming from a zip, and `status`, `knownCheckout` and `ResolveSource` handle that marker.
  - The REQUIREMENTS R8/R9 text as approved; ADR-038; the README map and the delivery docs; `AGENTS.md` rule 1.
  - Then item 7: the matrix lists, and the v1.8.0 release.
- **Out:**
  - fetching anything;
  - verifying the zip's signature, since a zip is unsigned and trust rests on the operator's own download;
  - replacing the binary from a zip;
  - item 6 of the pasted proposal;
  - a manifest schema change.
- **Follow-ups noted, not built:**
  - **A signed zip:** `/preflight` would publish a `git archive` zip under the release's signed `SHA256SUMS`, and `--from-zip` would verify it through the existing `ssh-keygen` path, refusing or clearly flagging an unverified zip. It changes R9's Release procedure, so it needs the operator's approval. Until then the command prints `UNVERIFIED` (security reviews r1 and r2, medium, open by decision).
  - `skills/find-skills/SKILL.md:97` names `example-harness` in a vendored skill: an old in-place edit, found during the item-4/5 sweep.

## Surfaces touched

- `internal/harness/zip.go` (new): `UnpackZip`. `internal/harness/zip_test.go` (new).
- `internal/harness/source.go`:
  - `ZipPrefix`;
  - a `Source.Origin` field the manifest records instead of `Dir`, when set.
- `internal/harness/apply.go:117-123`: the manifest's `Repo`/`Commit` for a zip source.
- `internal/harness/repo.go:75`: the `ResolveSource` candidate walk skips a `ZipPrefix` manifest value, as it skips `EmbeddedPrefix`.
- `cmd/sh-agent/main.go`:
  - the flag (`:84-90`);
  - the `reorder` value table (`:617`);
  - the usage string;
  - the `update` case (`:198-230`), with a `--from-zip` branch placed before `ResolveSource` (`:123`);
  - `status` (`:346-472`, the `from` line `:382-385` and the drift block `:444-471`);
  - `knownCheckout` (`:573`).
- `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go`: the CLI tests.
- `REQUIREMENTS.md` R8 and R9 (approved text); `.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md` ADR-038.
- `README.md`: § How it works (the map) and the install and update sections. `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/delivery.md` § How a machine gets the harness and § The model. `.agents/docs/deploy/{local,remote}.md` where they state the number of ways. `AGENTS.md` rule 1 ("Two ways in").
- `.agents/docs/testing/skill-matrix.md` (item 7).

## Interfaces

- **The command.** `sh-agent update --from-zip <file> [--home <dir>] [--vendor <v>] [--dry-run]`. `--from-zip` takes a value and joins `reorder`'s value table.
  - `--from-zip` with `--check` or with `--repo` is refused before anything is read: "--from-zip installs the named zip; --check/--repo do not apply to it".
  - `$SH_AGENT_REPO` is ignored on this path. The operator named the file, so D15 holds.
- **Order of work.**
  1. `sha256` of the file.
  2. `cfg, err := harness.ConfigDir(home)` (it returns an error too), then `harness.UnpackZip(file, cfg)`, which returns the tree's directory.
  3. `IsRepo(dir)`; failing it is an error naming the zip.
  4. `src := harness.Source{FS: os.DirFS(dir), Dir: dir, Origin: harness.ZipPrefix + "sha256:" + hex}`.
  5. `installFiles(src, home, vendor, dryRun, out)`, the same helper `install` uses: the running binary via `selfExecutable`, never `Reinstall`.
  6. `os.RemoveAll` of the unpack directory in a `defer`, on every path, errors and dry run included.
- **Output.**
  - First line: `zip <file> (sha256 <hex>): installing its harness with the running binary <version>; the binary itself is not replaced`, or the same with a `[dry-run]` prefix.
- **`harness.UnpackZip(zipPath, parent string) (dir string, err error)`**
  - It creates `os.MkdirTemp(parent, "zip-*")`.
  - It reads the archive with `archive/zip`.
  - Checks run at two scopes (D6).
    - **Archive-wide, on every entry:** the name must be relative, contain no `..` element and no backslash, and be `filepath.IsLocal` after cleaning. The archive may hold at most 5,000 entries. A breach refuses the whole zip, with nothing installed and the temp directory removed.
    - **Only on entries under the five extracted trees:** a symlink or any non-regular, non-directory mode refuses the whole zip. So does more than 16 MiB uncompressed for one file, or more than 128 MiB in total across the extracted files, counted from bytes actually written through an `io.LimitReader`, never from the header.
    - An entry outside the five trees is never opened and never written, whatever its mode. That includes this repository's own tracked symlink `.agents/skills`, which GitHub's zip keeps as a symlink entry.
  - **Layout.**
    - When every entry sits under one top-level folder and that folder holds `context/AGENTS.md`, the folder is stripped. That is GitHub's "Download ZIP" (`example-harness-main/…`) and its API zipball (`<owner>-<repo>-<sha>/…`).
    - Otherwise, when `context/AGENTS.md` is at the root, the root is used.
    - Otherwise the error is "not a harness zip: no context/AGENTS.md at its root or under one top folder".
  - **Extracted:** only entries under `context/`, `skills/`, `agents/`, `commands/` and `rules/`, the five trees the binary embeds. Every other entry is still name-checked, but never written.
  - File mode `0o644`, directories `0o755`.
- **`State.Repo` for a zip install:** `zip:sha256:<hex>`. `State.Commit` is `""`. `ZipPrefix = "zip:"`.
  - In `Install` (`apply.go:117-123`, which today branches on `src.Dir != ""` only), `src.Origin != ""` is checked FIRST and wins: `repo, commit = src.Origin, ""`. Then comes the existing `Dir` branch (path plus commit), and then the embedded branch. A zip source sets both `Dir` (the temp directory) and `Origin`; the temp path must never reach the manifest.
  - `ResolveSource` (`repo.go:75`) skips it as a candidate.
  - When `ResolveSource` finds no tree and the manifest's `Repo` has `ZipPrefix`, the not-found error (`repo.go:87`) gains, first: "this home was installed from a zip (sha256 <first 12 hex>); a development build needs a checkout or --repo — or run `sh-agent update --from-zip <file>` again". The rest of the message is unchanged (D7).
  - `knownCheckout` (`main.go:573`) treats it like `EmbeddedPrefix`: "this home was installed from a zip (sha256 <hex>), not from a checkout; pass --repo <dir> to build and install from it".
- **`status` for a manifest whose `Repo` has `ZipPrefix`.** `status` moves `harness.LoadState(home)` (today at `main.go:370`) to the top of the function, before the `source`/`repo` line (`:349-368`), so that line can append the zip note. The `installed nothing` early return keeps its place and message after the source line.
  - `installed  <time> from zip sha256:<first 12 hex> (…)`.
  - The drift block is replaced by a presence check over the manifest's files: `drift      not compared — installed from a zip that is not kept; <n> of <m> manifest files present`, then `  missing  ~/<rel>` for each absent one. The exit status is 1 when any is missing, 0 otherwise.
  - The `source` line for a release binary adds: `; this home was installed from a zip — run update --from-zip <file> again to change it`.
- **REQUIREMENTS, exactly as approved.**
  - R8's first sentence is replaced by: "The harness reaches a machine one of three ways: a checkout the operator owns; a release's `sh-agent` binary with the harness built in; or a zip of the repository that the operator downloads with their own credential and passes to `sh-agent update --from-zip <file>`. Each is kept current with `sh-agent update`: the checkout and the binary as today, and a zip place by the operator repeating the download and `--from-zip`."
  - R9's Install/Update procedure gains, as an indented sub-bullet under **Update** (D9), not as a fifth top-level procedure: "**Zip place:** the operator downloads the repository zip by hand and runs `sh-agent update --from-zip <file>`. It unpacks the zip into a temporary directory, refuses any entry that would leave it, installs that tree with the running binary, and deletes the directory. Nothing is fetched, no repository is created, and the binary itself is not replaced."
  - Both keep their approval notes: "(Approved by the operator 2026-09-28, on the exact text above: "approve as written"; ADR-038.)".
- **ADR-038.** A third way in, the zip place.
  - It supersedes ADR-034 for this one path only: a release binary installs a tree on disk solely when the operator names a zip with `--from-zip`, never a recorded or discovered path.
  - It amends the "two ways, no third" claim in `delivery.md`.

## Failure modes

- **Not a zip, or corrupt.** Error: "<file>: not a readable zip: <err>". Nothing is installed, the temp directory is removed, and the exit status is non-zero.
- **An unsafe entry** (slip, symlink, over a limit). The error names the entry and the rule it broke. Nothing is installed and the temp directory is removed.
- **Not a harness zip.** The error says so, and names the expected layout.
- **The zip carries a harness that needs a newer binary.** The install proceeds with the running binary; the first output line says the binary is not replaced. When the zip's `skills/` or `agents/` use something this binary cannot map (for example an unmapped tool in `derive.go`), the existing plan error stops the install before any write. That is the existing guard, unchanged.
- **The temp directory cannot be created** (unwritable `~/.config/sh-agent`). Error, and nothing installed.
- **`status` after a zip install** reports presence, not content. Content drift against the zip cannot be computed; the output says so rather than pretending.
- **A zip-installed home, then a development build with no checkout nearby and no `--repo`.** `status`, `diff`, `list`, `render` and `install` fail as they do today for a development build with no tree, and the error names the zip install (D7). A release binary never hits this: its source is its embedded files.
- **Dry run.** It unpacks and plans, prints what would change, and removes the temp directory. It writes no installed file, no manifest and no binary.

## Verification

- **Tiers:**
  - unit (`zip_test.go`: zip fixtures built in the test with `archive/zip`'s writer);
  - CLI (`main_test.go`);
  - an e2e with a real GitHub zip, using a release-versioned build;
  - security review (input parsing, a new way in);
  - `/review --docs`;
  - `TestHarnessMap`, which pins verbs; `--from-zip` is a flag, but the map gains a line.
- **E2E criteria:**
  1. **Golden path.** A binary built with a canonical release version runs `update --from-zip <GitHub zipball of main> --home <scratch>`. It installs, `status --home <scratch>` names the zip and reports every manifest file present, and the installed `~/.claude/AGENTS.md` equals the zip's rendered context.
  2. **Edge case.** A zip with an entry `x/../../escape` is refused, nothing is written under `<scratch>`, and no `zip-*` directory is left under `<scratch>/.config/sh-agent/`.
  3. **Dry run.** It leaves `<scratch>` byte-identical to before (manifest absent or unchanged), with no `zip-*` directory left.

## Phases

- [x] Cold-reader check — rounds 1–3 (`reviews/2026-09-28-coldread-update-from-zip-r{1,2,3}.md`); round 3 ended at the cap with one narrow residue (R9's structure), put to the operator, whose answer was "Go with your recommendations" (2026-09-28): D9

### Phase 1 — Zip source (internal/harness)

- [x] `UnpackZip` with the layout rules, limits and refusals — verify: `go test -race -run 'TestUnpackZip' ./internal/harness`, AI — expect: tests for GitHub top-folder strip, root layout, `..` slip, absolute name, backslash name, symlink entry INSIDE `skills/` (refused), symlink entry OUTSIDE the five trees such as `.agents/skills` (accepted, not written), over-count, over-size (written bytes), not-a-harness, and "entries outside the five trees not written" all pass. Each is written first and seen failing against a zero-value `UnpackZip`.
- [x] `ZipPrefix`, `Source.Origin`, the manifest record (`apply.go`), and the `ResolveSource` skip — verify: `go test -race ./internal/harness`, AI — expect: a test that an `Origin` source records `zip:sha256:…` with an empty commit, and that `ResolveSource` never returns a `zip:` manifest value as a candidate.
- [x] Checkpoint — expect: `go test -race ./...` green, gofmt and vet clean — evidence: `verifier` log `testing/2026-09-28-verify-update-from-zip-phase-1.md` PASS (139/266 pass; the must-fail mutation compiled and failed `one_file_too_large`; coverage 80–100% on the new functions, with uncovered error branches named), 2026-09-28. **No commit at this checkpoint:** the path change lands in ONE commit with its docs and map (`AGENTS.md` rule 3; D2).

### Phase 2 — CLI, status, knownCheckout

- [x] `--from-zip` flag, the `reorder` table and usage; the `update` branch before `ResolveSource`; the `--check`/`--repo` refusals; dry run — verify: `go test -race -run 'TestUpdateFromZip' ./cmd/sh-agent`, AI — expect: golden path into a scratch home; refusals; dry run writes nothing and leaves no `zip-*` directory (asserted absent, not only "normal mode present"); a release-versioned run installs from the zip, not the embedded files. — docs: `README.md` § update
- [x] `status` zip lines and presence check; `knownCheckout` zip branch — verify: `go test -race -run 'TestStatusAfterZip|TestKnownCheckoutZip' ./cmd/sh-agent`, AI — expect: the `from zip` line, "not compared" with the present count, missing files listed with exit 1, and the `knownCheckout` refusal text.
- [x] Checkpoint — expect: the full suite green — evidence: `verifier` log `testing/2026-09-28-verify-update-from-zip-phase-2.md` PASS (mutations (a) dry-run and (b) status both compiled and failed their named tests; restored identical), 2026-09-28. No commit (D2).

### Phase 3 — Requirements, ADR, docs, map, e2e, one commit

- [x] `REQUIREMENTS.md` R8/R9 exactly as approved; ADR-038 — verify: `git diff REQUIREMENTS.md`, AI — expect: only the two approved passages and their approval notes.
- [x] `AGENTS.md` rule 1 ("Two ways in" → three); `documentation` updates `README.md` (map and install/update), `delivery.md` § The model and § How a machine gets the harness, and `deploy/{local,remote}.md` pointers — verify: `/review --docs` over the phase diff, and `go test -run TestHarnessMap ./...`, both — expect: no restatement of the old count left. `git grep -niP '\btwo ways\b|\bno third\b|only way the harness|\bways in\b|one of the ways'` (`\b` because a bare `ways in` matches "always include") over the living docs (`README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `context/`, `skills/`, `agents/`, `.agents/docs/{specs,deploy}/`, `.agents/docs/testing/guide.md`) prints only lines that state the new three-way model, plus `skills/golang/references/golang-samber.md:431` ("two ways to compose operations", unrelated). Positive control: the same grep at the pre-feature HEAD prints `README.md:182` and `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md:61` among its hits. The map shows the zip line. — docs: `README.md`, `delivery.md`
- [x] E2E 1–3 — verify: a release-versioned build (`-ldflags "-X main.version=v0.0.1"`) in `.agents/scratch/`; the zip from `gh api repos/example-org/example-harness/zipball/main`; hand-built slip and dry-run cases; AI — expect: the three criteria above. Proven before trusting: the zip has one top folder, and the slip fixture holds the `..` entry (`unzip -l`).
- [x] `security` over the feature diff; `reviewer` over the diff — expect: findings fixed or rebutted in `## Outcome`.
- [x] Checkpoint — expect: ONE commit carrying the code, tests, REQUIREMENTS, ADR-038, docs and map; pushed — evidence: `verifier` log `testing/2026-09-28-verify-update-from-zip-phase-3.md` PASS; the feature commit follows this tick; 2026-09-28.

### Phase 4 — Matrix (item 7) and release

- [x] `testing/skill-matrix.md`: restore the lists the scenarios need (`bash`, `python3`, `curl` for Claude; the matching named agy commands), keep `edit_file(*)` and `list_dir(*)` out, and state that the allowlist lets scenarios run and is not a security boundary, because the sandbox runs as the operator's OS user; the protection is the throwaway home, with the copied token deleted by name after each batch — verify: read against the v1.8.0 gate code review's findings 1–3 (`reviews/2026-09-28-review-v1.7.0-381e86d-code.md`), AI — expect: each finding closed or rebutted.
- [x] `/preflight v1.8.0` over `v1.7.0..HEAD` — expect: VERDICT SHIP; tag, binaries, notes.
- [x] Checkpoint — expect: the release published; handoff written — evidence: the gate report path and release URL, <date>.

## Risks

Assumptions:
- GitHub's API zipball and the web "Download ZIP" both have exactly one top folder. Checked by `unzip -l` on the fetched zipball, the first task of the Phase 3 e2e.
- `archive/zip` exposes a symlink entry through `FileInfo().Mode()&fs.ModeSymlink`. Checked by the symlink unit test's fixture, whose `Mode()` is asserted before the refusal is tested.

## Decisions

- D1 — 2026-09-28 — Unpack under `ConfigDir(home)` (`~/.config/sh-agent/zip-*`), never `/tmp`. This follows the code's convention (`apply.go` `Diff`, `release.go` downloads), and a scratch `--home` keeps tests inside the scratch tree — by: implementer.
- D2 — 2026-09-28 — Phases 1–3 commit once, at the end of Phase 3. `AGENTS.md` rule 3 puts a path change in ONE commit with the code, docs and map, so the feature skill's per-phase commit is waived for these phases. The plan file and verify logs hold the state between them — by: implementer, per `AGENTS.md` rule 3.
- D3 — 2026-09-28 — No manifest schema change. The marker is a `State.Repo` value (`zip:sha256:<hex>`, the `EmbeddedPrefix` precedent), and `status` reports presence instead of content for zip installs. A new manifest field is what the repo's versioning rule calls MAJOR — by: implementer.
- D4 — 2026-09-28 — Extract only the five embedded trees. Name-check every entry, write only those. The zip also carries `.agents/`, `cmd/` and `internal/`, which the install never reads — by: implementer.
- D6 — 2026-09-28 — The symlink, mode and size checks apply only to entries under the five extracted trees; name safety and the entry count apply archive-wide. Otherwise the repo's own GitHub zip, whose `.agents/skills` is a tracked symlink, would be refused — by: cold read round 1 (`reviews/2026-09-28-coldread-update-from-zip-r1.md`, finding 1).
- D7 — 2026-09-28 — `--from-zip` works from any binary. Afterwards, a development build with no checkout and no `--repo` has no source for the other commands; they fail with the existing not-found error, which then names the zip install first. It is not given a way to read the manifest as a source, because nothing of the zip is kept. The zip place's intended binary is a release binary (R8), whose source is its embedded files — by: cold read round 2 (`reviews/2026-09-28-coldread-update-from-zip-r2.md`, finding 1).
- D8 — 2026-09-28 — The existing plain-copy path (an unpacked tree installed by a binary built from it; `update` refuses it) stays exactly as it is, the fallback `delivery.md` already describes. `--from-zip` is the zip place's way in and forward. The docs name both and say which is which: a zip place keeps no tree, while a plain copy is a tree someone unpacked and keeps — by: cold read rounds 1–2, finding 3.
- D9 — 2026-09-28 — The zip text sits inside R9's existing Update procedure, as a nested sub-bullet with the exact wording approved. It is a new kind of place, not a new procedure, so R9's "Four procedures" title and ADR-031 stay true. ADR-038 says so — by: the operator, "Go with your recommendations", on cold read round 3's residue (`reviews/2026-09-28-coldread-update-from-zip-r3.md`).
- D10 — 2026-09-28 — A dry run unpacks under `~/.config/sh-agent/` only when that directory already exists, and otherwise under the system temp directory. `ConfigDir` creates the directory, which a dry run must not do — by: implementer, Phase 1.
- D11 — 2026-09-28 — Supersedes the Interfaces lines on the output, `UnpackZip`'s signature, and "`--from-zip` with `--check` or `--repo` is refused", as well as D10's place of directory creation. It follows the review round (`reviews/2026-09-28-review-update-from-zip-{code,docs}.md`, `reviews/2026-09-28-security-update-from-zip.md`):
  - `UnpackZip(zipPath, parent) (dir, sum string, err error)` reads the file once (at most 256 MiB), hashes and parses that one buffer, and validates everything before writing: names (at most 1,024 bytes, fewer than 32 levels), count, kinds, duplicates, and sizes counted by decompressing. Only then does it create the parent chain, and on any error it removes everything it created.
  - `--from-zip` is detected with `fs.Visit` and refused before ANY command runs, when used with a command other than `update`, with an empty value, or with `--check`/`--repo`.
  - The first output line says `UNVERIFIED`, and that the running binary is installed but nothing in the zip replaces it.
  - `diff` does not compare a zip install.
  - A real run sweeps `zip-*` directories older than an hour.
  - `update --dry-run`, on the checkout and release paths, is its `--check`: it reports and changes nothing.

  — by: code review REQUEST CHANGES findings 1–3 and lows; security lows 2 and 3; docs lens 1–3.
- D12 — 2026-09-28 — The approved R9 sentence "the binary itself is not replaced" is imprecise: the running binary is installed as in every install; what holds is that nothing in the zip replaces it. REQUIREMENTS is not edited without the operator's approval, so the docs and output say the precise thing, and the sentence is put to the operator in the release report — by: implementer, from security review low 3.
- D13 — 2026-09-28 — Supersedes D11's "creates the parent chain … removes everything it created" inside `UnpackZip`, following round 2 (`reviews/2026-09-28-review-update-from-zip-code-r2.md`, `reviews/2026-09-28-security-update-from-zip-r2.md`):
  - `UnpackZip` no longer creates any directory beyond its own `zip-*`. `updateFromZip` creates `~/.config/sh-agent` with `MkdirAllTracked` and removes what it created on ANY failure, the install's own refusals included (BUG-093, third layer).
  - The sweep matches `zip-` names from `os.ReadDir` and never globs; a glob built from `--home 'h[1]'` reached another home.
  - The archive cap is 64 MiB.
  - Every zip CLI test runs with an empty `PATH` and a scratch working directory (BUG-094).

  — by: code review r2 findings 1–3; security r2 lows 2–3.
- D5 — 2026-09-28 — Item 7 takes matrix option 1 (the recommendation), read from "go all but number 6" on a row whose recommendation named the matrix choice — by: implementer, stated to the operator in chat.
- Rejected:
  - reading the zip in place as an `fs.FS` with no unpack: the approved REQUIREMENTS text says it unpacks into a temporary directory;
  - routing through `update()`/`Reinstall`: that rebuilds, and the scope forbids it;
  - per-file hashes in the manifest: a schema change (D3).

title: Research — memory for Antigravity, and `prompt-audit` for both CLIs (2026-09-29)
body:
# Research — memory for Antigravity, and `prompt-audit` for both CLIs   (2026-09-29)

## Questions

The operator asked, 2026-09-29: (1) "Do some broader research on internet and github if you find anything for antigravity" — memory, knowledge and "dreaming" features or plugins for the Antigravity editor and the `agy` CLI; (2) "do a check if there are a ./claude-api prompt-audit that we can implement for agy and claude in this harness." Light mode: research, compare, recommend. Follow-on to `plans/2026-09-29-dream-skill.md`.

## Answer in brief

1. **Antigravity has no memory feature the harness can use, and nothing to adopt.** The editor generates Knowledge Items (auto-extracted at conversation end, viewable in the Agent Manager, stored under `~/.gemini/antigravity/knowledge/`), but the feature has no docs page (the one Google staff linked now 404s), two forum threads report it never firing, and the CLI does not expose it: no docs, no help entry, no settings key, and on this box `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/knowledge/` holds only a lock file. Every community memory project for agy runs on hooks, a daemon, or a cloud service, which the harness rules out; the two hook-free ones re-do what the trail already does. Recommendation: nothing; the dream plan stays Claude Code only, and the trail is agy's memory.
2. **`prompt-audit` exists and can run on both CLIs.** It is a subcommand of Anthropic's `claude-api` skill: one 47 KB reference file, Apache-2.0, that audits prompts and agent configuration files (`AGENTS.md`, rules, skills, commands, subagents) for dated patterns and stale or contradicting instructions, and produces a report plus a proposed diff, never applying. On Claude Code it is bundled and runs today as `/claude-api prompt-audit`; agy has no copy. Recommendation: vendor the reference into a harness skill `prompt-audit` (option 2 below) so both CLIs run the same audit over `context/`, `agents/`, `skills/`, `commands/` and `rules/`, with the bug index as provenance.

## Part 1 — Antigravity memory

### What exists (verified 2026-09-29)

| Surface | Finding | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Editor (Antigravity 2.0) Knowledge Items | Auto-extracted from conversations; no setup; viewable in the Agent Manager; on disk as `~/.gemini/antigravity/knowledge/<item>/` with `metadata.json` and `artifacts/` | launch blog 2025-11-18; Google staff on the forum 2026-03-03; two export tools that read the directory |
| Editor KIs, reliability | Two forum threads (Dec 2025 to May 2026) report KIs never generated; escalated as a possible bug, no resolution posted | discuss.ai.google.dev threads 111234, 126774 |
| Editor KIs, docs | No docs page; `antigravity.google/docs/knowledge` is a 404; the docs nav has no Knowledge or Memory entry | fetched 2026-09-29 |
| CLI (`agy` 1.2.13) | No memory feature: docs overview and changelog say nothing; `agy --help` has no memory verb; `settings.json` has no memory key. The binary links the editor's Knowledge Base code (`KnowledgeBaseItem`, `GetUserMemories`, `GetCascadeMemories`, `knowledge_base_enabled`); `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/knowledge/` exists with only `knowledge.lock` (created 2026-09-17, never written); `cli.log` never mentions knowledge | this box, `strings $(which agy)`, `agy changelog` |
| CLI, its own summaries | `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/conversation_summaries.db` exists; one community project (`agy-dreamer`) reads it as its consolidation input | this box; github.com/j-steve/agy-dreamer |
| CLI plugin system | `agy plugin install <path>` (local path; the help also says `plugin@marketplace`), `import` from gemini or claude, `link <mp> <target>`; a plugin is `plugin.json` plus `skills/`, `agents/`, `rules/`, `mcp_config.json`, `hooks.json`. The marketplace is in-app (editor v2.18.1, 2026-09-28); no CLI marketplace verb documented; no memory plugin named in it | antigravity.google/docs/plugins; `agy plugin help` |
| Google announcements 2026 | I/O 2026 introduced the CLI; changelog through editor v2.18.1 and agy 1.2.13 has hooks (v2.11.0, agent-declared hooks v2.17.0) and the marketplace, and zero entries on knowledge, memory, learning or consolidation. No "dreaming" exists or is announced | changelog, I/O post |

### Community projects (GitHub, web-only survey; stars as shown on 2026-09-29)

| Project | Mechanism | Needs | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| thedotmack/claude-mem (94.9k★) | `~/.gemini/config/hooks.json` (5 events) + MCP + `GEMINI.md` injection | hooks + local Node worker daemon | agy hooks target 1.2.1; several open schema-breakage issues; editor support closed "not planned" |
| Mem0 plugin v0.3.1 | PreInvocation / PostToolUse / Stop hooks + MCP `search_memories` + 6 skills | hooks, cloud API key, Python 3.10+ | no consolidation |
| mahirocoko/agy-memory-layer (2★, v1.23.0 2026-09-27) | plugin with PreInvocation / PreToolUse hooks; skills `/dream`, `/remember`, `/palace`; git-backed `~/.gemini/memory/` | hooks | `/dream` is regex by default, LLM reflection only by hand; human-gated |
| atlaso-labs/antigravity (0★) | SessionStart / PreInvocation / Stop hooks + MCP + skill + rules | hooks, Atlaso cloud | — |
| Digital-Process-Tools/claude-remember (186★) | hooks; Haiku-compressed session → daily → weekly summaries | hooks | no SessionEnd analogue on agy |
| HydStAn/agy-memory-engine (34★) | MCP + hooks → SQLite FTS5 | hooks + worker every 5 min | — |
| j-steve/agy-dreamer (0★) | cron 03:00 reads `conversation_summaries.db`, writes `~/.gemini/config/dreaming/` | cron daemon | closest to "dreaming"; three commits |
| nowledge-co, blackmoon87/antigravity-mem | hooks + MCP + daemon | server or daemon | — |
| thevisionhub/agent-sleep (1★) | MCP tool `agent_sleep_consolidate` | MCP server only | hook-free |
| feodus/antigravity-memory-bank (9★, 2025-12) | rules + markdown files autoloaded in planning mode | nothing | hook-free; the trail (`handoffs/`, `bugs/`, `retros/`) already is this |

### Comparison

| Approach | Pros | Cons | Complexity | Cost | Maturity |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A. Nothing; the trail is agy's memory; re-check the CLI store after updates | no new store, no hooks, no daemon; matches project rule 1 | agy carries nothing across sessions beyond what a session reads from the trail | none | none | the trail: in use since 2026-09-03 |
| B. A hook-based plugin (claude-mem, Mem0, agy-memory-layer, claude-remember) | real capture across sessions | hooks and a daemon or cloud key; a second store beside the trail and Claude's auto memory; agy hook schema still breaking | medium | daemon or API key per machine | claude-mem mature on Claude Code, fragile on agy |
| C. A hook-free consolidation (agent-sleep MCP, or a harness skill reading `conversation_summaries.db`) | no hooks | reads an undocumented sqlite the CLI owns; an MCP server to run; nothing writes back into a store agy loads | medium | low | one to three commits each |
| D. Wait for the CLI's own Knowledge Base | first-party, code already linked in | undocumented, no switch, editor version unreliable | none now | none | not shipped |

### Recommendation: A

Nothing to adopt. Every real option needs hooks (project rule 1 and the global no-hooks rule) or a daemon; the hook-free ones duplicate the trail. The dream plan's Out section stands: the skill reads Claude Code's store only. Two lines to keep: re-check `ls ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/knowledge/` after each agy update (already in the dream plan's Risks), and note that `conversation_summaries.db` is the input a future CLI-side consolidation would read, if the operator ever wants one.

## Part 2 — `prompt-audit`

### What it is

- A subcommand of Anthropic's `claude-api` skill (github.com/anthropics/skills, `skills/claude-api/`, Apache-2.0 per its `LICENSE.txt`). The bare invocation `/claude-api prompt-audit` reads `shared/prompt-audit.md` and executes it. On Claude Code the skill is bundled with the CLI (session-scoped extraction; this session's copy is at Claude Code 2.1.283). agy has no copy: it is not a plugin and not in any agy marketplace.
- The reference is one file: 47,233 bytes bundled, 48,983 bytes upstream at commit `8a1541c` (2026-09-29; the upstream adds Claude Sonnet 5.5 rows). It cites `shared/model-migration.md` twelve times and `shared/prompt-caching.md` once, all for API request code (which model 400s on which parameter). For a configuration repository those rows are `not applicable`; the file says so itself ("a configuration repository mostly Groups 1 and 2").
- What it does, in order: establish scope and target model without asking; inventory every file that reaches the model (`AGENTS.md`, rules, skills and their references, commands, subagent definitions); `git blame` for provenance ("which failure, on which model, did this prevent"); classify every line ("could the model already know this?"); scan four groups: dated prompt text (pressure language, scaffolds, over-specification, fossils, prohibition clusters), brittle configuration files (volatile paths and flags, contradicting files, history narratives, recency-trap rules), tool descriptions, request config; then a report (`file:line`, evidence, pattern, why obsolete, confidence, action) and a proposed diff, one finding per hunk, never applied unless the request said so. A keep list protects context, exact scripts for fragile operations, prohibitions against demonstrated failures, and working redundancy.

### Fit with this harness

- **The shape matches.** The harness is a configuration repository: `context/AGENTS.md` (21,539 of 22,000 bytes, ADR-035), seven agents, 27 skills, commands and rules. Group 2 ("brittle skill and configuration files": volatile paths, contradicting files, one session's stumble as a permanent rule) is the harness's known failure mode: BUG-095 and the 2026-09-28 retro were four review rounds over rules that contradicted their neighbours.
- **Provenance is on disk.** The audit's central question per prohibitive line is which failure it prevents. Here every such line is meant to trace to a `bugs/INDEX.md` row or an ADR; keep-list item 5 then protects it, and a line with no row is the finding. A quick signal count: `never` appears 29 times in `context/AGENTS.md` and 23 in `agents/verifier.md`; caps-lock boosters (MUST, NEVER, ALWAYS, CRITICAL, IMPORTANT) zero times in any of them.
- **Two target models, not one.** The reference reasons about Claude's documented behaviour. The files it would audit here are read by Claude Code and by Gemini on agy. A finding grounded only in Claude's behaviour ("current models are proactive by default") is `flag`, not `remove`, until it holds for both; a stale-fact or conflict finding (Group 2) is model-independent and stays actionable. This is the one adaptation the harness wording must add.
- **What it cannot do here:** Group 4 (request config, API fossils) has no surface in this repository; the twelve `model-migration.md` cross-references are unreachable in a vendored copy and matter only for that group.

### Comparison

| Approach | Pros | Cons | Complexity | Cost | Maturity |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Claude Code only: run `/claude-api prompt-audit` as bundled, record the report in `reviews/` | zero harness change; always the current Anthropic text | not on agy; the bundled copy moves with the Claude Code version, so two machines audit against two texts; the two-model caveat lives nowhere | none | none | shipped |
| 2. Vendor the reference as a harness skill `prompt-audit` (thin `SKILL.md`, `references/prompt-audit.md` verbatim at a pin, `LICENSE.txt`, row in `VENDORED.md`) | same audit on both CLIs; pinned text, updated on purpose; the harness `SKILL.md` adds scope, provenance and the two-model rule; report goes to `<docs-root>/reviews/<date>-prompt-audit.md` | a 47 KB reference to re-vendor at each pin; a fork by the vendoring rule (the harness `SKILL.md` is the fork, the reference stays verbatim) | one sitting: file drop, `VENDORED.md` row, skill-matrix row, one behavioural run per CLI | none | upstream: active, Apache-2.0 |
| 3. A `/review --prompts` lens dispatching `reviewer` with the reference | reuses the review record and the report-only contract | `reviewer` runs on sonnet with a fixed report template the audit does not fit; the audit is judgment-heavy over the harness's own rules and wants the main model; adds a lens to a 66-line skill | medium | none | — |
| 4. Install the `claude-api` plugin on agy (`agy plugin import claude`, or a marketplace link) | whole skill, not one file | 1.8 MB, 79 files, most of it SDK code guides the harness never needs; `agy plugin install` takes a local path only per the docs; plugin import is untested here and the harness rules say a skill is deployed by `sh-agent install`, not by a vendor's plugin system | medium | none | untested |

### Recommendation: 2 — decided: option 3 (operator, 2026-09-29)

The operator chose option 3, a `/review --prompts` lens; built the same day (`changes/2026-09-29-1251-review-prompts-lens.md`). The reference is vendored under `skills/review-standards/references/prompt-audit/`, not a new skill.

Vendor `prompt-audit.md` verbatim (pin `8a1541c`, Apache-2.0, `LICENSE.txt` beside it) under `skills/prompt-audit/references/`, with a harness `SKILL.md` that says: scope is `context/`, `agents/`, every skill under `skills/` not in `VENDORED.md`, `commands/` and `rules/`, or the paths the user names; provenance comes from `bugs/INDEX.md`, `DECISIONS.md` and `git blame`, and a prohibition with a row is keep-list item 5; the target is both vendors, so a Claude-only rationale is `flag`; Group 4 is `not applicable` here; the report is written to `<docs-root>/reviews/<date>-prompt-audit.md` and nothing is applied. Run it by hand, and from `/retro` when a model release lands (the reference's own re-audit trigger). It is the only option that gives agy the audit at all, and the harness already has the vendoring path for it (`VENDORED.md`, the `anti-ui-slop` precedent for a bundled licence).

What approving it would do: a Task under the Definition of Done (one sitting, no design question left): the skill directory, the `VENDORED.md` row, a `skill-matrix.md` row, `sh-agent install` into a scratch home, one behavioural run per CLI on a fixture with a seeded contradiction and a seeded dead path (expect both found, nothing applied), `/review --docs` over the range, then a first real run over `context/` with the report in `reviews/`, put to the operator hunk by hunk.

## Not proposed

title: Plan — fyr: Antigravity only, no report path, renamed (2026-10-24)
body:
# Plan — fyr: Antigravity only, no report path, renamed   (2026-10-24)

## Why
The operator (2026-10-24, their own turn): "I want to remove claude from example harness fully. Only focus example harness on agy and I want to rename it to something else." Then: "lets go with fyr. I also want to rename the example-harness to fyr and then remove the report back to example-harness-feedback repo. This should be removed also." `fyr` is Swedish for lighthouse, the fixed light a vessel steers by; the name check (GitHub, Homebrew, Debian, PyPI, npm, crates, DNS, the web) is in the conversation of 2026-10-24 and found no developer tool, company or package of weight; trademark registers were not checked. Recon: `plans/2026-10-24-recon-agy-only-fyr.md` (Claude Code in ~22 non-test Go files, ~340 test mentions; `report.go` 1,102 lines plus 1,584 of tests; `sh-agent` 491 mentions in 60 Go files and 88 in 20 skills; ~5,000 lines deleted or edited; the trail stays as history). Memory `agy-only-and-rename`; feedback log 2026-10-24T19:31:51+02:00.

## Scope
In: the harness installs into the Antigravity CLI only — every Claude Code path leaves the binary, the skills, the agents, the context, the rules, the test kits and the docs; `sh-agent report` and the `example-harness-feedback` path leave entirely (the redactor stays, for the dream); the project is renamed `fyr` in place — repository `github.com/example-org/fyr`, module `github.com/example-org/fyr`, binary `fyr` (`cmd/fyr`), state `~/.config/fyr/`, timer unit `fyr-dream`, marker `.fyr-noindex`, env `FYR_*` — with one release, `fyr` only, after which each installed place is reinstalled by hand once (D5a); the requirements rewritten for one CLI; one ADR (ADR-062) superseding ADR-025 and ADR-060 and the report half of ADR-047a, amending ADR-030, 033 and 038 (the binary's name; the report clause of 033), ADR-047 (R10's scope), ADR-058 and 058a (the Kickoff wording where it names `claude`) and ADR-061 (R0's "both CLIs") — all in `.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md` (D10).
Out: a replacement for the report path (experience stays on the machine; the dream's harness-target proposals wait under `~/.config/fyr/proposals/dream/harness/` for the operator's own hands — D4); Antigravity IDE paths (Known limits); rewriting the historical trail (`changes/`, `handoffs/`, `reviews/`, `bugs/`, `testing/20*`, old plans and ADRs keep the old names: append-only); a new feedback repository.
Follow-ups noted, not built: the skill-listing budget (`TestSkillListingBudget`, 19,500 bytes, Claude Code's listing) stays until an Antigravity run measures that CLI's listing, then the number and its two comments are revisited (D24); the EGM deltas (standards, naive-reader lens, `--drift`) from plan `2026-10-23-session-sized-work.md` Phases 3–4, re-queued as their own plan after this one lands (D6); the resume-cost item (`bugs/INDEX.md` read whole) stays in that plan's Follow-ups.
Terms: EGM — the elephant-goldfish-model document standards and review lenses, plan `2026-10-23-session-sized-work.md` Phases 3–4 and `plans/*research-egm*`; Kickoff — the handoff's `## Kickoff` block (`skills/handoff/SKILL.md`); the canary — the last word of the deployed context, asked for by a behavioural run (`testing/guide.md` § 4); the preamble's three lines — what `testing/kit-preamble.sh` prints before a run; R-parity — REQUIREMENTS R10; § 3, § 3a, § 3d, § 3g — sections of `testing/guide.md` (§ 3a is the plain-copy tier, where `IsCheckout` in `internal/harness/source.go` is false); `ab-kit`, `seed-security`, `agy-rel` — run kits under `.agents/docs/testing/`; BUG-079 — `bugs/BUG-079-*` (a binary shadowed on PATH; `pathguard.go`); the resync — `Install`'s removal of files the previous manifest listed and this plan does not (`internal/harness/apply.go:122-146`).

## Surfaces touched
Recon brief `plans/2026-10-24-recon-agy-only-fyr.md` §§ 1–5 (file:line anchors and counts). Go: `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` (verbs, `--vendor`, `runReport`, uninstall's `RemoveKeptClone`), `internal/harness/{plan,settings,derive,report,release,repo,state,pathguard,sweep,apply,source,inventory}.go` and tests, `embed.go` (package `example`), `go.mod`, `internal/metrics/{claude,ingest,show,report,events,store}.go`, `internal/dream/{dream,collect,run,timer}.go`, `internal/memory/memory.go`, `internal/search` (`.sh-agent-noindex`, store path). Content: `context/AGENTS.md` (3 Claude Code mentions: lines 31, 39, 64), `rules/`, `agents/*.md` (8, format per D3), `skills/init-project` (26 mentions; the stub list and the `.claude/*` links), `handoff`, `feedback-log`, `project-memory`, `review`, `preflight`, `dream`, `google-catalog` router text, `skills/VENDORED.md`. Docs: `README.md` (the map, verbs table, install), project `AGENTS.md` (rules 1–6, layout, setup), `REQUIREMENTS.md` (R0, R1, R2, R7, R8, R9, R10, Non-goals), `ROADMAP.md`, `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/{delivery,search,metrics,memory-loop}.md`, `deploy/{local,remote}.md`, `testing/{guide.md,kit-preamble.sh,ab-kit,seed-security,agy-rel,skill-matrix.md,sh-agent-matrix.md}`. External: the GitHub repository rename (who: user), the releases, `example-harness-feedback` (archived or deleted, who: user), each installed place (`deploy/remote.md` § The four places).

## Interfaces
- **Binary and paths.** `fyr <verb>`; verbs `install`, `update [--from-zip]`, `uninstall`, `status`, `diff`, `sync`, `list`, `render`, `version`, `adopt`, `search`, `index`, `memory`, `metrics`, `dream`, each unchanged but for the name — `report` gone; `--vendor` gone (one vendor); `--home DIR` stays (R6). State `~/.config/fyr/` with the same files (`state.json`, `search.db`, `metrics.db`, `feedback.jsonl`, `retros.jsonl`, `proposals/`, `reports/`, `dream/`); `metrics.Path`, `state.go`'s five paths, `dream` paths all read one constant `StateDir = ".config/fyr"`. Timer unit `fyr-dream.{service,timer}`, launchd `com.fyr.dream`. Project marker `.fyr-noindex`, with `.sh-agent-noindex` still honoured (D12). Env `FYR_HOME`, `FYR_REPO`, … (today's `SH_AGENT_*`, one for one); a set `SH_AGENT_*` variable is not read and gets one notice naming its `FYR_*` name (D15). Module `github.com/example-org/fyr`, root package `fyr` (today `example`), `cmd/fyr`.
- **Migration (D13, D14).** One function runs first, before anything opens the state dir, in every verb that writes under it (`install`, `update`, `sync`, `adopt`, `uninstall`, `index`, `search`, `memory add`, `metrics ingest`, `dream`): when `~/.config/fyr` is absent and `~/.config/sh-agent` exists, is a directory and not a symlink → `os.Rename` it to `~/.config/fyr` and print `migrated ~/.config/sh-agent → ~/.config/fyr`; when both exist → leave both, print one line naming them, and use `~/.config/fyr` (F3). The read-only verbs and modes (`status`, `diff`, `list`, `render`, `version`, `memory show`, `metrics show|report|export`, `install --dry-run`, `update --check`) never migrate: with only the old dir present they print one line, `run fyr install to migrate ~/.config/sh-agent`, and read nothing from it. Because `install`'s resync reads the previous manifest from the state dir, the migration precedes it, and the resync then removes the old manifest's entries the new plan does not name: the Claude Code files (`~/.claude/AGENTS.md`, the `CLAUDE.md` stub, `~/.claude/{agents,skills,rules}/*`) and `~/.local/bin/sh-agent` when the old install wrote it (`plan.go:188-190`, `selfExe`), by today's rule only — a symlink or a path under a link is the operator's and stays (`apply.go:136-139`), and a removal error stops the install as today (F2). No new removal rule is written. `~/.claude` itself stays in `pruneEmptyDirs`' stop map, so emptying it never deletes the directory. The dream timer: `install` replaces an installed `sh-agent-dream` systemd unit or `com.example.sh-agent-dream` launchd job with `fyr-dream` / `com.fyr.dream` (disable the old, enable the new) and says so, through BUG-144's `UnitFor(home)` suffix scheme for both names. `~/.claude/settings.json` is never touched again (the two keys stay as the operator's; the handoff names them for by-hand removal).
- **The crossing, by hand (D5a).** `v3.0.0` is cut from the renamed repository and publishes `fyr-<os>-<arch>`, the zip and `SHA256SUMS` with the one marker `# fyr v3.0.0`; no `sh-agent-*` asset, no shim, no second marker. An old binary's `sh-agent update` therefore fails on the asset name (F1) and the place is reinstalled by hand once, the procedure in `deploy/remote.md` § Crossing to fyr: release-binary place — `gh release download v3.0.0 --repo example-org/fyr --pattern fyr-<os>-<arch>`, `chmod +x`, `./fyr install` (which migrates `~/.config/sh-agent`, removes `~/.local/bin/sh-agent`, sweeps the old manifest's files, installs itself); checkout place — `git remote set-url origin git@github.com:example-org/fyr.git`, `git pull --ff-only`, `go run ./cmd/fyr install`; zip place — download the `fyr-<os>-<arch>` asset by hand as a release-binary place does, `chmod +x`, then `./fyr update --from-zip <zip>` (a plain-copy install copies the running `./fyr` to `~/.local/bin/fyr`, `plan.go:188-190`; the zip itself replaces no binary, R9) (D19). At every place the operator also rewrites or removes any unit or profile line of their own that names `sh-agent` — on the dev box the hourly `sh-agent-update.timer` (`deploy/remote.md` § the timer example), which fails today because the v2.7.0 release binary refuses `--repo` — and renames any exported `SH_AGENT_*` variable (D11, D15). `sh-agent uninstall` is NOT run first: it would delete the state the migration carries. Four places, all the operator's (`deploy/remote.md` § The four places), each ticked in Phase 6 by name.
- **Agents (D3).** Authored natively as `agents/<name>/agent.md` in Antigravity's format (the keys `DeriveAgy` writes today: name, description, subagent, mainAgent, model, tools); `derive.go` is deleted; the lint keeps the tool allow-list (`toolMap` becomes `knownTools`: an unknown tool name still fails the install, Known limits) and the frontmatter allow-list (ADR-056; `agentKeys` becomes Antigravity's keys). `install` copies `agents/<name>/agent.md` to `~/.gemini/config/agents/<name>/agent.md` unchanged. The authored files are today's derived output: each is byte-equal to what `DeriveAgy` writes for that agent at the Phase 3a base commit (the test), so model values (`pro`, `flash`, omitted), tool names (`view_file`, …) and body paths are whatever derivation produces now; `knownTools` is the set of values in today's `toolMap`; the `## Installed` inventory prints the agent's `model` key as written, or nothing when absent. Phrases "a budget below the agent's `maxTurns`" in the context and skills become "a tool-call budget the dispatch names" (D17).
- **Redactor.** `Redact`, `RedactJSONL` and the needle lists move from `report.go` to `internal/redact` with their tests (`TestReportRedactShapes` renamed, every needle's benign near-miss kept; project `AGENTS.md`'s needles rule points at the new file); `internal/dream/collect.go` imports it.
- **Metrics (D7).** `metrics ingest` reads Antigravity only; `show`, `report` and the dream summary keep their one-column shape with `agy`; rows with `cli=claude` already in a store are left in place and shown under a `claude (historical)` column only when present (no deletion of operator data); `metrics export` writes them as before.
- **REQUIREMENTS.md (Phase 0, exact text proposed there, approved by the operator before Phase 1).** R0 "the second brain of the Antigravity CLI"; R1 "One source, one vendor" (agents authored in Antigravity's `agent.md` format, nothing derived); R2 keeps the agents.md standard and drops the stub list and "Claude Code 2.1.277+ reads AGENTS.md natively" (a project has `AGENTS.md` alone, which Antigravity reads natively); R4 `fyr`; R7 drops "never sent by `sh-agent report`"; R8 "One delivery channel, and it is `fyr`" with the Report-back bullet gone from R9 (three procedures: install, update, release); R10 "One behaviour on every machine" (the parity clause becomes: every place behaves the same; the Known-differences table in memory-loop.md is retired); Non-goals: the settings.json bullet becomes "Editing any vendor setting: the harness is files in the customization directories, nothing else" (the three exceptions go with Claude Code); plus R3, R5, the title, and Known limits 2 and 3 with one row added (D18); the exact set is `.agents/scratch/fyr/requirements-edit.md`.
- **README map (rule 3).** The amber "report back" line and the `example-harness-feedback` node leave; the three ways in stay with the new names; the dreamer's olive dashed line stays; `TestHarnessMap` (`cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go:1399`, moved with the package) pins the new verb set and refuses `report`. Rule 1 of the project `AGENTS.md` becomes "Three ways in, no way back"; rule 6's one home, `delivery.md` § The model, is rewritten in the same commit.

## Failure modes
- F1 An old place runs `sh-agent update` after `v3.0.0` exists → today's code finds no `sh-agent-<os>-<arch>` asset (or, on a checkout, `go build ./cmd/sh-agent` finds no such package) and replaces nothing (today's rule); the place follows `deploy/remote.md` § Crossing to fyr by hand. Before `v3.0.0` exists, today's behaviour.
- F2 `fyr install` at a crossing: `~/.local/bin/sh-agent` is a symlink or under one, or was never in the old manifest → it stays (today's resync rule) and `fyr status` names it (F4); its removal fails (`os.Remove` error) → the install stops with the error as today, the operator removes the file by hand and runs `fyr install` again (D14).
- F3 `~/.config/fyr` and `~/.config/sh-agent` both exist at install → neither is touched; one line names both and says which one `fyr` reads (`~/.config/fyr`); the operator merges or removes by hand.
- F4 Both `sh-agent` and `fyr` on PATH after a crossing that left the old file (F2) → `fyr status` prints the `shadowed`-style line naming the leftover (BUG-079's path, extended to the old name).
- F5 The GitHub rename: `gh` API reads and `git` remotes follow the redirect until a repository named `example-harness` is created again under the account — the plan forbids that, in `deploy/remote.md`; a checkout place's `origin` is changed by hand (`git remote set-url`, § Crossing to fyr), never by `update` (D16).
- F8 A file under a directory that carries the old marker `.sh-agent-noindex` → still left out of every index (D12); a test with only the old marker proves it.
- F6 An agent file in the old Claude Code format left under `agents/` → the lint refuses the install naming the file (Phase 3a's test).
- F7 A project with a `.claude/` link tree made by the old `/init-project` → `fyr` ignores it and the skill no longer makes or removes one; the links are the operator's to delete (D16).

## Verification
Tiers: unit (`go test -race -count=1 -timeout 30m ./...`, gofmt, vet, govulncheck by full path); scratch-home install (§ 3, Antigravity paths only) and the plain-copy tier (§ 3a: `IsCheckout` logic untouched but the binary name changes); § 3d (search: the marker rename) and § 3g (metrics: agy-only ingest, historical rows) rows; behavioural runs on Antigravity for every changed skill and agent (preflight's rule; the eight agents change format under D3, so eight runs plus the changed skills — `skill-matrix.md` rows on agy only), each with the kit preamble's three lines; the crossing on a scratch "place" before the release: a home holding `~/.config/sh-agent`, `~/.local/bin/sh-agent` and an old manifest, migrated by one `fyr install` built from the tree (Phase 4b's checkpoint); the real places after the tag (Phase 6, who: user).
